title: Adaptive Chaos-Based Parameter Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel parameter optimization technique based on adaptive chaos theory. Traditional parameter optimization methods often rely on static parameter settings, limiting their ability to adapt to complex, dynamic datasets. We introduce an algorithm that dynamically adjusts parameters based on the input data using an adaptive chaos model, offering a more intelligent and flexible approach to parameter selection. This method aims to enhance optimization performance by proactively responding to changing data patterns. The core mechanism involves establishing a chaotic system and iteratively modifying its parameters to achieve a desired optimization outcome. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and evaluation, demonstrating its potential for improved parameter selection in various optimization scenarios.

title: "CertiView"
abstract: "Reliable auditing is critical for detecting silent failures in deployed machine learning services before they affect downstream decisions. However, existing label-free methods can report reassuring accuracy estimates even when a model is consistently wrong, because observable prediction behavior does not by itself determine semantic correctness. In this paper, we introduce CertiView, a selective auditing framework that queries one black-box classifier through multiple label-preserving views. We first state that accuracy is not identifiable from a single view or from general two-view observations. We then establish sufficient conditions under which three views identify the class prior and each view\u2019s asymmetric confusion matrix up to permutation. A semantic alignment condition resolves this remaining ambiguity and recovers accuracy. CertiView estimates the identifiable model through spectrally initialized likelihood optimization. Additional views create overidentifying constraints that reveal model incompatibility. We further state a perturbation bound for deviations from the ideal assumptions. Finally, CertiView converts its uncertainty assessment into a risk-controlled decision and abstains when reliable auditing cannot be supported."

title: Quantifying the Experience of Difficulty: Behavioral and Trajectory Applications for Adaptive Systems
abstract: Many digital systems do not track behavioral metrics that are associated with perceptions of difficulty; however, this perception is an important driver of engagement and learning. The goal of this project was to identify metrics of problem-solving and determine their relationship with subjective difficulty perception. We modeled move-by-move progression through logic puzzles and found that revisiting prior moves and general problem-solving efficiency predicted both subjective difficulty and objective performance. Interestingly, path volatility, caused by a variety of deviations from the optimal path to the solution, uniquely predicted subjective difficulty perception. Using these markers may enable the design of more responsive systems that detect user struggle and prevent attrition.

title: Dr. Claw: An AI Scientist Workspace for Vibe Research
abstract: Command-line coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Gemini CLI) can already read and write files and sustain long sessions, yet end-to-end research still fragments across chat tools, IDEs, terminals, and writing environments, and the decisions that make it auditable are rarely preserved. We present Dr. Claw, an open-source workspace that wraps existing coding-agent executors in a controllable and auditable human-in-the-loop workflow rather than introducing another autonomous agent. Persistent state objects, a reusable skill library, and multi-executor coordination link human decisions to AI execution, turning planning, execution, and writing into one traceable, recoverable loop. We demonstrate Dr. Claw through an interactive three-view scenario and a failure-recovery walkthrough, and evaluate it against a bare command-line agent sharing the same backend executor, so the comparison contrasts the whole orchestration layer (task graph, state objects, and skill library) with the agent it wraps. Holding the executor fixed, Dr. Claw scores higher on research completeness while persisting an auditable, recoverable process trail. Demo access: repository https://github.com/OpenLAIR/dr-claw, released under AGPL-3.0 with GPL-3.0 upstream components.

title: Do General NLP Embeddings Capture Ontological Reasoning?
abstract: General-purpose NLP embedding models perform well on linguistic tasks, but their ability to capture symbolic ontological structure remains unclear. We introduce AVA, a systematic framework for evaluating whether embeddings distinguish logic-sensitive relational semantics in ontologies and knowledge graphs. AVA comprises 171,007 contrastive triplets derived from 163 heterogeneous ontologies using hierarchy inversion, relation substitution, and disjointness injection. Each triplet contains an ontology statement, a semantically equivalent paraphrase, and a logic-sensitive hard negative with contradictory relational meaning. We evaluate more than 25 state-of-the-art embedding models and find substantial limitations: the best model achieves only 0.739 triplet accuracy, while hard negative accuracy falls to 0.135. Fine-tuning improves discrimination by a large margin but transfers poorly to downstream Semantic Web tasks, including taxonomy discovery and ontology alignment. Further analysis suggests that improvements stem partly from perturbation-specific pattern recognition rather than robust ontological understanding. These findings reveal a persistent gap between linguistic representation learning and ontology-level discrimination, challenging the assumption that strong NLP benchmark performance translates to Semantic Web competence.

title: Reciprocity Separates Gradient Flow from Rotation in Conservative Physical Learning
abstract: Physical learning lets a trainable material or network use its own physical response to carry error signals, reducing the need for a separately programmed backward computation. We ask what determines whether such a system follows conventional gradient descent or evolves along a genuinely different learning trajectory. Our canonical model is a directed layered transport network in which every node redistributes a fixed amount of flow, so learning preserves positivity and total mass. In this model, conservation constrains only the allowable learning directions. Within the matched response class studied here, adjoint matching gives the physical output response a symmetric form. Non-negative mode-wise feedback then produces a reciprocal closed-loop response and a reweighted gradient flow. Adding an antisymmetric boundary component makes the closed-loop response rotational: the learning path can turn while the error driving that update still decreases at that moment. Turning is not automatically beneficial. Its finite-step effect is set by local curvature, and its accumulated effect also depends on step selection and on the new states visited along the path. Numerical consistency checks reproduce the exact response structure, predict the sign of the local effect across new network families, and show how trajectory drift can negate a local advantage. These results separate the roles of conservation, reciprocity, and nonreciprocity in physical learning.

title: Learning Radio Astronomical Representations with LeJEPA and Very Small Models
abstract: Representations learned by vision foundation models pretrained on natural images have been shown to be useful for out-of-domain astronomical images. Performance on scientific downstream tasks increases with model size, which both carries higher inference costs and limits scalability, even when considering parameter-efficient adaptation. An alternative is to learn representations directly from astronomical observations rather than natural images, through self-supervised pretraining. We evaluate LeJEPA's ability to learn robust representations using very small vision models ($\sim$6M parameters) pretrained on Radio Galaxy Zoo images, comparing with established self-supervised frameworks. We test whether LeJEPA's latent-space regularization leads to better radio galaxy morphology classification. Across three evaluation datasets, LeJEPA achieves performance comparable to a substantially larger foundation model while producing more consistent representations across training and evaluation datasets. These results suggest that the choice of representation learning objective is critical for enabling small domain-specific models to achieve performance competitive with representations transferred from large foundation models in scientific imaging.

title: Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions along vector fields
abstract: We investigate diffusion approximations for a class of multivariate inhomogeneous finite-velocity random motions motivated by models of active particles. A particle alternates cyclically among prescribed velocity fields V_1,dots,V_p with random run times and evolves according to either a flight dynamics, consisting of piecewise-linear motion, or a gliding dynamics, in which the particle follows the corresponding velocity flow. Under a Kac-type scaling that couples vanishing run times with diverging particle speed, we prove weak convergence of both processes to multidimensional diffusions. It turns out that the order of successive cyclic motions affects the diffusion limit. In addition to the second-order term generated by fluctuations of the random run times, the limiting drift contains directional derivatives DV_i[V_j] of the underlying vector fields. In Stratonovich form, part of this drift is expressed through their Lie brackets [V_i,V_j]. Thus, the generic non-commutativity of the microscopic motions survives the diffusive scaling and generates a macroscopic drift which depends on the cyclic order. The limiting drift also distinguishes the flight and gliding dynamics, despite their being driven by the same vector fields and run times. Several examples, including run-and-reverse motion and cyclic dynamics generated by multiple vector fields, illustrate how the cyclic switching protocol and the geometry of the underlying velocity fields shape the limiting diffusions.

title: Messages Passed Along the Edges: A Historical Development Review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of GNN and graph learning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Filosofía ESTROMÁTICA de la Computación cuántica
abstract: El futuro que se esboza no es el de una máquina omnisciente ni el de una simple aceleración de lo ya conocido. Es el de una nueva capacidad para generar conocimiento sobre regímenes de la naturaleza y de la matemática que hasta ahora permanecían opacos. Esa capacidad solo se realizará plenamente en la medida en que el sujeto operatorio continúe tejiendo, con rigor material, con ambición conceptual y con responsabilidad histórica, las tramas que hacen posible el tránsito de lo posible a lo efectivo. En ese tejido —denso, discontinuo, codeterminado— reside la verdadera profundidad filosófica de la computación cuántica.

title: The Remaining Construction, Constructed: A Closed-Form Twiddle for the 24-Cell Quantum Reader and a Semidirect-Product Fourier Obstruction
abstract: The parent paper [1] reduced the circuit synthesis of the optimal 24-outcome reader for the binary tetrahedralgroup 2T to the synthesis of a single fixed operator: the 2T group Fourier transform F, whichblock-diagonalizes the regular representation into irreducible blocks [1,1,1, 2,2,2, 2,2,2, 3,3,3]. That paperreported, as an honest negative (its Result D), that the naive tensor product FC3 ⊗ FQ8 fails to realize F,because 2T = Q8 : C3 is a crossed (semidirect) product, and it named the missing piece — the twiddle fromthe Clifford theory of Q8 : C3 — as a remaining construction. Here we construct it. We show (i) the twiddle hasan exact closed form: in coset-times-fiber coordinates, each two-dimensional-sector column of F equals (ωmM0)t applied to the Q8-Fourier column, where M0 is the intertwiner of the two-dimensional irrep ρ with itsC3-conjugate (rebuild residual 1.7 × 10-16); (ii) a semidirect-product Fourier obstruction: nodirect-product-form two-factor split of F exists, because the C3-action moves the Fourier dual of Q8 nontrivially(M0 ≠ I) — stated and verified as a direct-versus-semidirect contrast, not as an observed residual; and (iii) adirect measurement of the binary-embedding tax: the abstract group-FFT gate count is O(101), but ageneric-Givens emitter on the 24-into-32 five-qubit embedding cannot realize it, so the O(102) target isreachable in principle yet unreached with a structure-blind emitter. The line's firmly established compressionremains the parent paper's Lever-1 (25,210 → 5,980 CNOT, 4.2×). No quantum-advantage claim is madeanywhere. All results are exact statevector-level numpy computations at machine precision. ※The license for codes is AGPL3.0-or-later

title: 基于量子隐形态的图灵机验证 - 证明复杂系统安全性的理论框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for quantum-enhanced graph theory verification, specifically designed for validating complex systems. The core idea is to leverage quantum superposition and entanglement to simulate the behavior of these systems and utilize quantum algorithms for verification purposes. This approach aims to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of verification, offering a potential breakthrough for security analysis across diverse domains, including protein structure, chemical reactions, and more. The paper details the proposed mechanism, discusses the benefits and challenges associated with this quantum approach, and concludes with a preliminary assessment of its theoretical soundness and practical implications. We demonstrate a conceptual model and outline a pathway toward further exploration and refinement of this framework.

title: Topological Optimization of Quantum Circuits
abstract: This paper explores the potential of topological optimization for quantum circuit design. Traditional quantum circuit design relies heavily on classical optimization techniques, often leading to complex and error-prone circuits. This work proposes a novel approach leveraging the inherent properties of topological networks to minimize circuit complexity and reduce errors. The core concept involves mapping quantum circuits onto a topologically protected network, where the topological features inherently constrain and optimize the circuit layout. This approach aims to reduce qubit-qubit distances and unwanted interactions, thereby enhancing the robustness and scalability of quantum computation. The theoretical framework presented here outlines the key considerations and potential benefits of this topological optimization strategy. Further research and development in this area are anticipated to significantly impact the design and implementation of future quantum computers. ---

title: Secrecy in Squirrel and the Post-Compromise Security of a Ratchet
abstract: This repository contains the additional material for the paper"Secrecy in Squirrel and the Post-Compromise Security of a Ratchet",Clément Hérouard, Charlie Jacomme, Adrien Koutsos, Joseph Lallemand, CCS 2026. ## Organization The artifacts include:- `case-studies/`: the Squirrel developments (see below for details);- `squirrel-prover/`: our secrecy logic extension of Squirrel;- `docker/`: configuration and script to build the Docker image;- `squirrel-secrecy.tar`: pre-built Docker image. ## HTML Files The case studies can be browsed through without installing anyadditional software using the HTML proof exports in`case-studies/html_reports/`. For each case study, this directorycontains a corresponding HTML file that allows to interactivelyre-execute the proofs step by step by clicking on the proof lines toexecute. These files only display in an interactive way the output previouslyproduced by Squirrel on a given Squirrel input file, but do not re-checkthat the proofs are correct -- they are provided for convenience, but do notconstitute a proof in themselves.These exports are static and do not allow to interactively modify the proofs. ## Case Studies The main claims of the papers can be found in the following places: - `case-studies/asym-ratchet/` contains the asymmetric ratchet case study of Section 5 (cf. corresponding README). - `case-studies` also contains the Squirrel model and proof for the motivating example of Section 2 (`motivating-example.sp`), as well as a small introductory tutorial teaching basic manipulations of the secrecy predicate (`weak_secrecy_tuto.sp`); - `squirrel-prover/theories/WeakSecrecy.sp`, which has been integrated inside Squirrel's standard library, notably contains proofs for some soundness rules (Theorem C.2 and C.3). ## Reproduction with Docker Provided that docker is[installed](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install), the followinginstructions allow to reproduce our results: 1 - Load the docker image `squirrel-secrecy.tar` using `docker load --input squirrel-secrecy.tar`. Alternatively, the docker image may be built from scratch by running `./docker/build.sh`. 2 - Once the docker image is loaded, run `docker run -it sp/squirrel-prover-secrecy:latest bash`. 3 - Run all our examples by executing `make` in the `case-studies/` directory. Depending on the available ressources and currentdocker configuration,some case-studies may fail due to a timeout. If such a timeout occurs,one may go into the `case-studies/asym-ratchet` folder and then run `sed -i '1s/^/set smtSteps=10000000.\n/' model.sp` which adds a special configuration line in the model file. Re-running`make` should then succeed. ## Reproduction from Sources 1 - Build Squirrel. First build the Squirrel prover, whose source code is in `squirrel/`. See `squirrel/README.md` for dependencies and build instructions. Note that building with SMT support is mandatory for some of our examples. These developments were checked using CVC5 (version 1.0.8) and Z3 (version 4.13.2). 2 - Add Squirrel to the PATH. `export PATH=$PATH:/path/to/squirrel` 3 - Run examples. To run all our examples, execute `make` in the `case-studies/` directory.

title: Core Claim: Propose a self-adaptive parameter adjustment strategy for quantum topology model parameters to enhance model accuracy and performance.
abstract: Quantum topology is a rapidly developing field with the potential to revolutionize quantum computing and information processing. It leverages the unique properties of spacetime to create topologically protected quantum states, offering enhanced resilience against noise and decoherence. The accurate modeling of quantum topology is crucial for its successful implementation. However, current parameter estimation techniques often rely on traditional methods, which can be computationally expensive and may not fully capture the complex dynamics governing these systems. This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive parameter adjustment strategy for quantum topology model parameters, aiming to address these limitations and significantly enhance model accuracy and performance. The proposed strategy dynamically adjusts parameters based on observed model behavior, optimizing for both fidelity and stability. We explore a novel approach leveraging a Bayesian optimization framework combined with a reinforcement learning component to iteratively refine parameter values. Our results demonstrate a substantial improvement in model accuracy, particularly in the context of generating complex topological structures, compared to static parameter settings. Furthermore, the proposed method exhibits improved robustness and adaptability to varying input conditions. The design incorporates a mechanism for self-monitoring and error correction, ensuring the model remains well-tuned over extended simulations. This work represents a significant advancement in parameter estimation techniques tailored specifically to the challenges posed by quantum topology modeling. This results in improved model performance and opens up new avenues for research and development in this exciting field.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Probabilistic Activation Function Design
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has emerged as a transformative field, offering the potential to revolutionize various computational tasks. This paper explores the design of a novel quantum activation function based on probabilistic graphs, aiming to enhance machine learning model performance, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional data and non-linear relationships. We introduce a "probability graph embedding" mechanism to simplify computation and boost model expressiveness. The core claim is that this approach allows for more accurate representation of complex system dynamics and improved performance in challenging scenarios. This work proposes a new method for encoding and processing data, leveraging the inherent properties of probabilistic graphs to achieve a more robust and adaptable quantum machine learning system.

title: Core Claim: Establish a dynamically adaptable probability space, capable of adjusting parameter values based on data distribution shifts, thereby enhancing the precision of probabilistic models.
abstract: The pursuit of accurate probabilistic models often relies on sophisticated algorithms that require careful parameter tuning. This paper introduces a novel approach to probabilistic modeling – the Adaptive Probability Space (APS) – designed to dynamically adjust probability space parameters in response to changes in data distribution. The core principle behind APS is the continuous refinement of the probability space through iterative adjustments based on observed data. We propose a method for automatically identifying and responding to distributional shifts, significantly improving the predictive accuracy of probabilistic models compared to static approaches. This work addresses the limitations of current probabilistic modeling techniques by introducing a framework that prioritizes adaptability and enhanced precision. The benefits of this dynamic adaptation are highlighted through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples demonstrating improved performance on diverse datasets. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, including exploring more sophisticated parameter adjustment strategies and integrating APS with other machine learning paradigms.

title: Quantum Information Field Synchronization Algorithm (QISA)
abstract: Quantum Information Field Synchronization Algorithm (QISA) presents a novel synchronization protocol leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance the fidelity and efficiency of data transfer and synchronization between quantum and classical computing systems. This algorithm addresses the critical challenges associated with quantum error correction, distance limitations, and the inherent noise sensitivity of quantum systems. The core mechanism relies on establishing and maintaining entanglement between two or more quantum systems, allowing for instantaneous correlation and the manipulation of quantum states across distances. This approach offers a pathway to significantly reduce errors and improve the performance of quantum technologies, representing a significant advancement beyond current synchronization methods. This paper details the theoretical foundation, implementation, and experimental validation of QISA, highlighting its potential to revolutionize quantum information processing.

title: 基于多变量贝叶斯网络的因果推理学习
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to dynamic system understanding and prediction by leveraging multi-variate Bayesian Networks (MVBNs) and causal inference algorithms. The core idea is to transform MVBNs into executable causal inference models through causal embedding techniques, enabling both forward and backward causal reasoning and prediction. Unlike traditional methods reliant on static causal graphs, our framework addresses dynamic changes in causal relationships and integrates probabilistic modeling capabilities inherent in Bayesian Networks. We explore the theoretical underpinnings and outline a methodology for constructing and utilizing these dynamic causal models, aiming for a deeper understanding of complex system behavior. The key contribution lies in the ability to learn and adapt causal models from data, offering a robust solution for systems where causal relationships are not fully known a priori. This work provides a foundation for building more intelligent and adaptable systems capable of handling uncertainty and predicting future states with greater accuracy.

title: Non-Euclidean Chaos-Based Data Compression - Adaptive Entropy Encoding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel data compression algorithm, "Non-Euclidean Chaos-Based Data Compression," designed to achieve unprecedented efficiency through the application of principles of non-Euclidean chaos. The core concept revolves around identifying and exploiting subtle, unpredictable patterns within data through a probabilistic algorithm. This algorithm generates a compressed representation that mirrors the fundamental structure of the data, minimizing redundancy and maximizing information content. We detail the algorithm's structure, explain the rationale behind the chosen chaos-based approach, and present preliminary results demonstrating significant compression ratios compared to existing methods. The focus is on achieving a truly adaptive and efficient compression strategy, moving beyond traditional approaches.

title: Neural Networks with Probabilistic Logic
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network design by integrating principles from probabilistic logic. The core idea is to introduce probabilistic distributions within the connection weights of neural networks, effectively simulating probabilistic logic operations performed by neurons. This hybrid system combines probabilistic inference with logical deduction, offering enhanced capabilities for modeling nonlinear systems, particularly those dealing with uncertainty and ambiguity. We demonstrate how this integration can lead to more robust and accurate pattern recognition and decision-making processes compared to traditional neural networks relying solely on classical logic. The proposed framework addresses a significant limitation in current neural network architectures, expanding their applicability to real-world scenarios where data is inherently uncertain and incomplete. The key contribution lies in the ability to model complex systems directly, rather than relying on approximations or post-hoc processing of probabilistic outputs. ---

title: 多体量子场论的自适应几何建模
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for multi-scale quantum field theory modeling based on adaptive geometry. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters to accurately represent complex quantum field phenomena. The core mechanism involves introducing 'adaptive geometry' – a system of geometric transformations that responds to the dynamics of the underlying quantum field. This allows for the simulation of intricate quantum behavior, enhancing computational precision and facilitating advanced quantum information processing. The paper demonstrates the efficacy of this approach through illustrative examples, showcasing improved accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional static geometry-based models. We highlight the advantages of this self-adaptive approach in tackling challenging quantum systems.

title: Bicolored Tube-nosed Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bicolored Tube-nosed Bat" (BTNB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of *Rhinolophus clivosus*, a bicolored tube-nosed bat. These bats exhibit a unique foraging strategy characterized by alternating between short-range and long-range searches, guided by both local gradient information and global landmark recognition. The BTNB algorithm mimics these behaviors through a population-based search process, utilizing a color-coded representation of bat positions reflecting their exploration and exploitation tendencies. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic adjustment of bat movement ranges based on gradient information, mimicking the bats' shift between local and global searches. This paper details the algorithm's design, including the color representation, movement mechanisms, and convergence criteria. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy on a series of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and Sphere function, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The algorithm's performance is evaluated based on convergence speed and solution quality. Key results demonstrate the BTNB algorithm's potential for tackling complex, multi-dimensional optimization challenges.

title: Neuromorphic Computing with Spiking Neural Networks and Reservoir Computing for Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility of leveraging neuromorphic computing paradigms, specifically reservoir computing and spiking neural networks (SNNs), to achieve emergent symbolic reasoning. Traditional artificial neural networks struggle with representing and manipulating abstract concepts, a core requirement for symbolic reasoning. We propose a framework where a reservoir of randomly connected spiking neurons acts as a dynamic, high-dimensional space, processing input data and generating temporal patterns. A simple readout layer then learns to map these patterns to symbolic representations, potentially through mechanisms inspired by Boltzmann machines or trainable linear layers. The central hypothesis is that by carefully designing the reservoir and training the readout, we can induce the emergence of symbolic behavior, moving beyond simple temporal pattern detection. This work explores the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and outlines a potential architecture for achieving this goal. The investigation focuses on the interplay between the reservoir's dynamics and the readout layer's learning process, aiming to demonstrate how these components can collaborate to exhibit rudimentary symbolic reasoning.

title: Probabilistic Program Generation Based on Probability Models
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to program generation leveraging the power of probability models. The core idea is to represent the potential states and transitions within a program's execution using probabilistic graphical models, specifically Bayesian Networks. A program generator then utilizes these models to produce sequences of program execution steps through sampling and inference, leading to the generation of programs exhibiting non-deterministic behavior. Unlike traditional program generation techniques reliant on explicit rules and constraints, our method captures inherent program uncertainty, yielding more natural and adaptable program behaviors. This approach offers a pathway to automatically creating programs capable of handling complex, unpredictable scenarios without the need for manually encoding every possible situation. The research contributes to a new paradigm in program synthesis by combining probabilistic reasoning with program generation techniques.

title: Multi-Agent Simulation with Emergent Game Dynamics and Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This research explores the application of evolutionary algorithms within multi-agent simulation to foster emergent game dynamics. Traditional multi-agent simulation methods often fail to adequately represent the complex, unpredictable behaviors that arise from the interactions of multiple agents. This project proposes a framework where agents are subjected to a simulated environment and evolved using evolutionary algorithms. This process allows agents to adapt, learn, and develop sophisticated strategies directly from their interactions, leading to emergent behaviors that are not explicitly programmed. The core innovation lies in the integration of evolutionary optimization with agent-based simulation, offering a dynamic approach to modeling complex systems and promoting the discovery of novel strategies within the agent population. The simulation methodology is presented, focusing on the key components and parameters involved in driving the emergent dynamics.

title: Baja Pocket Mouse Optimization Algorithm (BPMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Baja Pocket Mouse Optimization Algorithm (BPMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Baja Pocket Mouse. The algorithm utilizes a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies mimicking the mouse's efficient search for food resources in a complex environment. BPMO employs a population-based approach, utilizing a swarm of agents that iteratively update their positions based on a local fitness landscape and global information. The algorithm incorporates mechanisms for velocity control, adaptive parameter adjustment, and a novel constriction heuristic designed to promote efficient convergence. The core of BPMO lies in a dynamic constriction parameter, denoted as *cd(t)*, which evolves over time to balance exploration and exploitation. The performance of BPMO is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive effectiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising candidate for various optimization challenges. Specifically, the algorithm's performance is demonstrated across continuous optimization problems, showcasing its ability to navigate complex landscapes and achieve optimal or near-optimal solutions. The key parameters of BPMO, including the swarm size (*N*), the constriction parameter (*cd(t)*), and the inertia weight (*w*), are identified as critical factors influencing the algorithm's convergence and solution quality. Future work will focus on incorporating BPMO into hybrid optimization frameworks and exploring its applicability to real-world engineering problems.

title: Authenticated Quantum Key Distribution Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a novel protocol for authenticated quantum key distribution (QKD) that addresses the inherent vulnerabilities of traditional, centralized key management systems. The core concept leverages the security of QKD to establish a shared secret key, then integrates this key with a classical authentication protocol to verify the identities of the communicating parties. The protocol, denoted as AQKD, aims to enhance overall communication security by combining the unique properties of quantum key distribution with robust classical authentication mechanisms. The design incorporates a multi-round key exchange utilizing Bennett-May-Crabtree (BMC) protocol and incorporates a challenge-response mechanism for authentication. The proposed protocol mitigates risks associated with compromised central servers and provides a more resilient security posture. The primary contribution lies in the synergistic integration of these two established cryptographic paradigms, resulting in a more secure and adaptable communication system. The protocol's security is analyzed, considering potential attacks and demonstrating its resilience. The simulation results highlight the effectiveness of AQKD in establishing secure communication channels, particularly against eavesdropping and identity forgery attempts.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum mechanics to constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) through a novel dynamic topology approach. The core mechanism leverages a quantum state representation that evolves based on the problem constraints, dynamically modifying the system's topology to guide the search process. This work presents a theoretical framework and preliminary simulations demonstrating the efficacy of this dynamic topology quantum CSP algorithm.

title: Design of a Quantum Memory Based on Quantum Demixing
abstract: Quantum memory is a crucial component for the development of quantum computing and quantum communication. However, the primary challenge in building a practical quantum memory lies in mitigating quantum decoherence, the loss of quantum information due to interaction with the environment. This paper proposes a novel quantum memory design leveraging the principle of quantum demixing, a phenomenon where interactions between quantum bits (qubits) can effectively slow down the decoherence rate. The design utilizes a carefully engineered architecture where qubits are coupled in a specific manner to promote entanglement and suppress unwanted dephasing. We explore the theoretical framework for this design, focusing on the mathematical models describing the decoherence process and the impact of qubit interactions. The core claim is that optimized quantum memory structures can significantly reduce decoherence, leading to enhanced storage capacity and read/write rates. This work presents a new approach to quantum memory design, addressing a fundamental limitation in the field. ---

title: Gravitational Wave Signal Reconstruction via Quantum Amplitude Amplification
abstract: Gravitational wave detection relies heavily on the detection of minuscule fluctuations in spacetime, requiring incredibly sensitive instruments. Current detectors, like LIGO and Virgo, face limitations in sensitivity due to inherent noise and signal-to-noise ratios. This paper proposes a novel quantum algorithm, Quantum Amplitude Amplification (QAA), designed to significantly enhance the probability of detecting faint gravitational wave signals, thereby improving the sensitivity of gravitational wave detectors. The core mechanism utilizes quantum amplitude amplification to enhance the probability of observing the desired gravitational wave signal, increasing detection rates. This research addresses a critical challenge in gravitational wave astronomy by exploring a fundamentally new approach to signal processing.

title: Ammodile: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the American Woodcreeper
abstract: This paper introduces Ammodile, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the American Woodcreeper (Dendrocolaptes auratus). Woodcreepers are known for their unique and efficient method of searching for insects on tree trunks, utilizing a combination of random movement and targeted exploration. Ammodile leverages these principles to develop a new optimization algorithm suitable for a wide range of problems. The algorithm employs a dynamic exploration-exploitation strategy, represented by two key parameters: the 'step size' (s) and the 'focus factor' (f). The step size dictates the randomness of the search, while the focus factor governs the level of targeted exploration. The algorithm's core loop involves generating a candidate solution (s_1, s_2, ..., s_K), evaluating its fitness, and adjusting the step size and focus factor based on a predefined rule. We demonstrate Ammodile's efficacy through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA). The algorithm's adaptability and relative simplicity make it a promising candidate for various applications. The primary contributions of this work are the conceptual framework for Ammodile and its demonstrated performance across several test problems.

title: Alpine Chipmunk: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Alpine Chipmunk Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Alpine Chipmunk, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of alpine chipmunks. The algorithm leverages the chipmunks' strategy of caching food items in multiple locations, prioritizing locations based on estimated food availability, and dynamically adjusting caching strategies based on environmental changes. Alpine Chipmunk employs a combination of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) techniques, incorporating a novel 'Cache Density' metric to guide particle movement and a 'Seasonal Adaptation' mechanism to adjust parameters over time. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive results against established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO, Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO). The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of caching strategies and the seasonal adaptation, mimicking the chipmunks' survival strategy in a fluctuating environment. The algorithm's key parameters, denoted as *ρ* (inertia weight), *c1* (cognitive coefficient), *c2* (social coefficient), *T* (temperature), and *α* (cache density), are described in detail. The results indicate that Alpine Chipmunk is a robust and efficient metaheuristic algorithm suitable for various complex optimization tasks.

title: # Allen's Striped Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Striped Bat Optimization" (SBO), inspired by the foraging behavior of Allen's striped bats ( *Lasiurus cinereus nebulosus*). These bats exhibit a unique hunting strategy involving synchronized movement and exploration of their environment. The SBO algorithm mimics this behavior to solve complex optimization problems. The core mechanism of the algorithm centers around a 'striped' representation of bat positions, utilizing a dynamic 'stripe intensity' to guide exploration and exploitation. The algorithm's parameters, including stripe intensity, bat velocity, and attraction/repulsion forces, are tuned based on the bat's observed foraging patterns. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's convergence properties and its adaptability to various problem landscapes. The algorithm is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithms (GA). The results indicate that the SBO algorithm is particularly effective in navigating complex, multimodal landscapes, demonstrating its potential for a broad range of optimization challenges. The algorithm's efficiency and robustness are highlighted, offering a promising alternative for tackling computationally demanding optimization tasks.

title: Agile Mangabey: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Agile Movements of Mangabeys
abstract: This paper introduces Agile Mangabey, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging and movement strategies of mangabeys, highly social primates known for their agile and adaptable behavior in complex environments. The algorithm leverages the mangabey's ability to quickly assess and react to changes in their surroundings, combined with their social dynamics, to achieve efficient exploration and exploitation within a search space. Agile Mangabey incorporates key elements such as a dynamic population size, adaptive step size adjustment based on environmental complexity, and a social interaction mechanism mimicking the cooperative foraging of mangabeys. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's mechanics, including the key parameters and their influence on performance. Empirical results demonstrate Agile Mangabey's effectiveness across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising approach for tackling complex optimization challenges. The core of the algorithm involves a dynamic population, where individuals' movement is governed by a combination of random exploration and adaptive exploitation, influenced by a 'complexity metric' derived from the search space. The social interaction component ensures that individuals learn from each other, promoting convergence and avoiding premature stagnation.

title: ## Black Fox Monkey Inspired Meta-Heuristic Optimization Algorithm (BFM-MHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Black Fox Monkey Inspired Meta-Heuristic Optimization Algorithm (BFM-MHOA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior and social dynamics of black-and-white colobus monkeys ( *Chlorocebus pygerythrus*). The algorithm leverages the monkeys' efficient exploration of complex environments, their tendency to cluster around high-reward food sources, and their adaptive social strategies to navigate challenges. BFM-MHOA combines elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO), simulated annealing (SA), and a novel 'social influence' component mimicking monkey group behavior. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the influence of individual best positions and the global best position within the swarm, based on a 'social cohesion' metric derived from proximity to other individuals. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundation, detailed implementation, and proposes a framework for future research and practical applications.

title: Quantum Information Geometry Modeling
abstract: Quantum Information Geometry Modeling explores the intersection of quantum information theory and geometric principles, aiming to construct robust and efficient quantum information protocols. This research investigates the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum geometry to enhance the security and efficiency of information transfer. The core mechanism involves establishing a mathematical foundation for quantum information, encoding data through entangled states, and developing a novel encryption algorithm based on quantum geometry. This work addresses a significant gap in current cryptographic practices by introducing a fundamentally new approach to secure communication.

title: Dynamic Arity Adjustment for Efficient d-ary Heaps
abstract: The d-ary heaps are among the most widely used implementations of priority queues.The arity d, which determines the number of children per node, is typically fixed throughout the execution of an algorithm, with values such as d = 2, 4, and 8 commonly used due to their simplicity, balanced performance between sift-up and sift-down operations, and cache efficiency.This paper observes that changing the arity from a larger value to a smaller value (e.g., 4 to 2) during execution can reduce the number of key comparisons in many priorityqueue-based applications.Based on this observation, we propose a method that dynamically adjusts the arity at an appropriate moment: the heap begins with a larger arity when sift-up operations dominate in the early phase and switches to a smaller arity as sift-down operations gradually dominate.We evaluate the proposed method both analytically and experimentally and show that it reduces the number of key comparisons by 3%-25% across a diverse range of applications and input workloads.The proposed method complements existing techniques for improving d-ary heaps and provides a practical approach to reducing priority-queue costs.

title: Integrated Multisource Geophysical and Remote Sensing Data Fusion for Mineral Prospectivity Mapping: A Reproducible Framework Applied to the Olympic Cu–Au Province, Gawler Craton, South Australia
abstract: Mineral exploration in covered and structurally complex terranes increasingly relies on the integration of complementary evidence layers rather than any single dataset. This study presents a reproducible, open-data workflow for mineral prospectivity mapping (MPM) that fuses multispectral and thermal remote sensing, potential-field and radiometric geophysics, and public geological and mineral-occurrence data within a common geographic information system (GIS) framework. The workflow combines knowledge-driven fuzzy logic, data-driven weights-of-evidence, and a machine-learning ensemble (random forest with gradient-boosted refinement) through a stacked meta-learner, and is validated using spatial k-fold cross-validation, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and prediction-rate curves referenced against independent occurrence subsets. We demonstrate the framework on the Olympic Cu–Au Province of the Gawler Craton, South Australia — a world-class, largely covered iron oxide copper-gold (IOCG) system for which regional gravity, aeromagnetic, radiometric, magnetotelluric, and geological data are openly available through national and state geoscience portals. Evidence layers derived from reduced-to-pole magnetics, residual Bouguer gravity, radioelement ratios, ASTERderived alteration indices, structural lineament density, and lithological favorability are standardized to a common 30 m grid and integrated using the proposed fusion architecture. Consistent with published mineral-systems studies of the province, structural and magnetic-gravity evidence layers emerge as the strongest predictors of IOCG favorability, with alteration and radiometric layers providing secondary but non-redundant discrimination. We discuss the comparative advantages of ensemble fusion over single-source and single-method approaches, the sensitivity of prospectivity outputs to training-occurrence bias, and the practical steps required to operationalize the framework using entirely open datasets. The methodology, code structure, and evidence-layer catalogue are provided to support reproducibility and transfer to other covered metallogenic provinces.

title: Innovative Design of Equipment with Artificial Intelligence Elements.
abstract: This publication presents the design principles of laser and optoelectronic systems and instrumentation operating under conditions where artificial intelligence (AI) and artificial neural network (ANN) elements are integrated into control, monitoring, and decision-support units, while also considering the prospective transition to quantum computing technologies and their functional equivalents. Particular attention is devoted to the development of integrated intelligent infrastructures that combine supersystems and interconnected subsystems into unified technological environments. The publication describes methods of real-time online monitoring based on the analysis of electromagnetic radiation characteristics, electrical resistance, and advanced high-speed resonance spectroscopy. These methodological approaches were developed by the well-known innovation specialist Aleksandr Neshin on the basis of his multidisciplinary professional experience in advanced airfield industrial complexes.The publication also examines the application of integrated automated assembly systems for electronic components, the use of high-torque micromotors operating on the principles of the inverse piezoelectric effect, and modern methods for monitoring the optical parameters of complex engineering systems through mobile digital applications and intelligent monitoring devices.Special consideration is given to manufacturing technologies for components, assemblies, instruments, and systems of various levels of complexity using industrial production equipment while maintaining the technical characteristics required for the classification of intelligent equipment and smart technological systems.The author particularly emphasizes the innovative scientific and engineering developments of Aleksandr Neshin, who formulated a systematic approach to the integrative implementation of artificial intelligence and artificial neural network elements in the design of Austrian Journal of Technical and Natural Sciences, 2026 No 7 -8 Section 5. Technical sciences in general smart home ecosystems and infrastructure, including advanced engineering solutions for large-area glazed structures and intelligent building components.The concepts presented in this publication demonstrate that laser and optoelectronic systems incorporating artificial intelligence and neural network technologies, together with the future integration of quantum computing principles, constitute a fundamental element of intelligent feedback systems designed for the monitoring, control, and adaptive management of next-generation smart engineering infrastructure.The publication highlights the practical significance of Aleksandr Neshin's multidisciplinary approach for the further development of intelligent technological systems, advanced engineering solutions, and innovative digital infrastructure.

title: Insolation Dynamics and Their Influence on Climate Variability in Northern Malaysia: A Case Study of Perlis
abstract: Solar insolation represents one of the Earth’s most important renewable energy sources. In Perlis, Malaysia, high levels of solar radiation are experienced year-round, with notable variations in weather conditions. These fluctuations play a significant role in shaping the region’s insolation patterns. Therefore, this study aims to explore the interdependency between weather variability and insolation patterns in Perlis, focusing on two main objectives: first, to examine seasonal variations in weather conditions, and second, to determine correlations between weather variables and insolation throughout the year. To achieve these objectives, the study begins with comprehensive data acquisition, where meteorological data are analysed to identify seasonal trends and fluctuations in weather conditions. At the same time, solar radiation data are carefully generated using a Digital Terrain Model (DTM), ensuring accurate representation of spatial variability. Following this, statistical analyses, particularly correlation methods, are applied to evaluate the relationships between key meteorological variables and insolation. The findings reveal that temperature and precipitation exhibit moderate correlations with insolation patterns, with coefficients of determination (R²) of 0.5549 and 0.5458, respectively. In contrast, wind speed shows only a weak relationship with insolation, indicated by a low R² value of 0.0537. Building on these results, Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques are employed to map the spatial distribution of both insolation and weather variables across the study area. Overall, the integration of statistical and spatial analyses provides a comprehensive understanding of how seasonal weather variations influence solar radiation in Perlis. These insights are valuable for supporting environmental management strategies and enhancing local-level planning and decision-making, particularly in the context of renewable energy development.

title: Risk-aware multiple-choice question answering with conformal P-values
abstract: Multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) systems are often required to act on uncertain evidence while still providing a concise decision to a user. We introduce a risk-aware MCQA interface that converts normalized option probabilities into conformal prediction sets, allowing the system to retain every answer option supported at a user-selected risk level. The option-wise conformal p-value provides an interpretable rank-based view of this decision. Across five instruction-tuned language models and common-question subsets of MMLU and MMLU-Pro, the procedure is evaluated with 100 random 1:1 calibration-test splits at target miscoverage levels [Formula: see text]. At [Formula: see text], mean empirical miscoverage ranges from 0.0390 to 0.0399 on MMLU and from 0.0469 to 0.0487 on MMLU-Pro; the same target-tracking pattern persists at the larger operating points and across diverse subjects. Prediction sets contract smoothly as the allowable risk increases, while the more demanding MMLU-Pro questions retain broader sets. These results position conformal p-values as a practical reliability layer for MCQA systems that must communicate calibrated ambiguity rather than conceal it behind a single top-ranked answer.

title: Construction and Application of a Time‐Series Sentiment Analysis Model for Online Learning: A Case of Online Teacher Training
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Online teacher training has emerged as a crucial pathway for professional development. However, the spatiotemporal separation inherent in online learning often gives rise to emotional challenges, including loneliness, fatigue, and reduced engagement, which can compromise learning outcomes. While prior studies recognize the value of emotion analysis and feedback, they typically rely on static or snapshot measures, limiting insights into the temporal evolution of learners' affective states and constraining timely interventions. Objectives This study aims to develop a time‐series sentiment analysis model that enables real‐time, automated monitoring and feedback of teachers' emotional states in online learning environments, thereby enhancing engagement, self‐regulation, and overall learning effectiveness. Methods A BERT‐based deep learning model was employed to classify textual sentiment, and an orthogonal polynomial regression approach captured temporal dynamics of affective states. The integrated model was embedded within an online Project‐Based Learning platform under a blended education framework. A sequential within‐subject quasi‐experimental design was adopted, combining questionnaire surveys and semi‐structured interviews, with Friedman tests and Wilcoxon signed‐rank post hoc comparisons used to assess the impact of time‐series emotional feedback on learners' online learning outcomes. Results and Conclusions The proposed model significantly improves online teacher training by sustaining engagement, reducing attrition risk, and supporting adaptive cognitive‐emotional regulation. Real‐time visualization and automated feedback facilitate timely interventions, enabling teachers to adjust strategies and maintain reflective learning practices. These findings demonstrate the potential of time‐series sentiment analysis to inform data‐driven, emotion‐aware design of online professional development, advancing both methodological innovation and practical applications in teacher training.

title: Estimating Population-Risk Curves Along Nonconvex Gradient Flows from the Training Sample
abstract: We estimate the conditional population-risk curve of a realized smooth nonconvex gradient flow from the training sample. Flow approximate leave-one-out (Flow-ALO) propagates a deletion response and evaluates omitted observations at approximate deleted paths. The risk-curve error decomposes into response approximation, exact-LOO fluctuation, and deletion-to-full risk transfer. On each fixed finite horizon, bounded centered training-loss gradients, a one-sided Hessian lower bound, locally Lipschitz Hessians, and a strict tube-closure condition yield an explicit $(n-1)^{-2}$ bound for the deletion-response error. Bounded evaluation-loss gradients transfer the deletion-response bound to the score without requiring the Hessian to be invertible. Direct first-order jackknife cancellation and exact-LOO concentration control deletion-to-full risk transfer and fluctuation, respectively, completing recovery of the conditional population-risk curve. For bounded smooth two-layer mean-field networks training both layers, the score-error bound is uniform in width.

title: Geometry-Grounded Unified 3D Perception for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Camera-based autonomous driving perception requires a shared representation that preserves metric 3D structure across synchronized multi-camera streams. However, existing image-based frameworks often rely on backbones pretrained for semantic recognition, and introduce 3D geometry through downstream task-specific modules. As a result, their shared representations may fail to preserve explicit metric geometry and consistent 3D scene structure. In this paper, we present a Geometry-grounded Unified 3D Perception (GeoUP) framework that adapts the reconstruction-oriented latent of VGGT to calibrated, streaming multi-camera driving scenes. GeoUP factorizes cross-image interaction into self, temporal, and view attention to capture structurally distinct temporal and cross-view correspondences. It further injects calibration-aware raymap encodings to provide metric scale and camera geometry. The resulting geometry-grounded latent is decoded for metric depth estimation, 3D object detection, and semantic occupancy prediction, corresponding to surface-, instance-, and volume-level readouts of the same 3D scene. Through joint multi-task and multi-dataset training, GeoUP effectively leverages heterogeneous annotations and generalizes across diverse sensor configurations and perception ranges. Extensive experiments on nuScenes, Argoverse 2, Waymo, KITTI, and DDAD demonstrate that GeoUP achieves SOTA performance across detection, occupancy, and depth estimation. These results validate the effectiveness of geometry-grounded representations for unified 3D driving perception.

title: From coupled Z 3 Rabi models to the Z 3 Potts model
abstract: We study a Z 3 -symmetric Rabi model that describes a three-level system coupled to two bosonic modes. We derive a mapping of the two-mode Z 3 Rabi model onto a qubit-boson ring. This mapping allows us to formulate a realistic implementation of the Z 3 Rabi model based on superconducting qubits. It also provides context for the previously proposed optomechanical implementation of the Z 3 Rabi model. In addition, we propose a physical implementation of the Z 3 Potts model via a coupled chain of Z 3 Rabi models.

title: Implementasi Chatbot AIML untuk Layanan Pelanggan UMKM Warung Kopi XYZ
abstract: UMKM Warung Kopi XYZ melayani penyediaan minuman, makanan ringan, dan fasilitas tempat berkumpul bagi pelanggan. Namun, pengelola dan barista sering menerima pertanyaan berulang mengenai menu, harga, lokasi, fasilitas Wi-Fi, hingga reservasi tempat, khususnya pada jam operasional sibuk dan akhir pekan. Penelitian ini mengembangkan chatbot berbasis web menggunakan Artificial Intelligence Markup Language (AIML) untuk menyediakan respons otomatis atas pertanyaan layanan pelanggan. Data kebutuhan diperoleh melalui wawancara dengan pengelola kedai, observasi percakapan pelanggan, dan kajian literatur. Pertanyaan pelanggan diproses melalui case folding, tokenisasi, pemeriksaan ejaan (spell checker), stemming, dan filtering sebelum pattern dicocokkan dengan knowledge base AIML. Sistem menyediakan peran pengguna (pelanggan) dan admin (pengelola kedai); pelanggan mengajukan pertanyaan seputar layanan kedai, sedangkan admin dapat menambah atau menghapus pattern serta meninjau riwayat percakapan. Evaluasi meliputi uji akurasi respons, System Usability Scale (SUS), dan black-box testing. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan akurasi 91,49% berdasarkan 43 respons sesuai dari 47 pertanyaan, skor SUS rata-rata 82 yang berada pada kategori good, serta keberhasilan 100% pada 36 skenario pengujian fungsional. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa chatbot AIML layak digunakan untuk mengurangi beban respons berulang pada UMKM kuliner, meskipun normalisasi salah ketik dan cakupan pattern masih perlu diperluas.

Furthermore, we analyze the potential benefits and challenges associated with this approach, including the required infrastructure and theoretical limitations.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology Optimization Algorithm
abstract: The field of quantum computing is rapidly advancing, driven by the potential for unprecedented computational power. However, efficient quantum algorithms require precise control over quantum systems, and current parameter optimization methods often struggle to find optimal configurations. This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum topology optimization algorithm that leverages the inherent properties of quantum systems to dynamically adjust parameters, ultimately leading to more efficient and robust quantum computations. We propose a mechanism for automatically tuning quantum system parameters based on the current state of the quantum system, significantly enhancing the optimization process compared to traditional approaches. This algorithm aims to address limitations in current parameter adjustment techniques and unlock new possibilities for quantum algorithm design. The core of the algorithm revolves around constructing and manipulating quantum topological states, allowing for a highly adaptable and efficient optimization strategy.

title: 基于多模态神经编码的认知架构
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cognitive architecture grounded in multi-modal neural encoding. The core idea is to represent human cognition by learning a unified multi-modal neural representation from diverse sensory inputs – visual, auditory, tactile, and physiological signals. This architecture leverages deep neural networks to establish intricate relationships between these modalities, ultimately generating a high-dimensional space where cognitive processes can be simulated and reasoned about. Traditional cognitive architectures often operate within the confines of single-modality data, limiting their ability to accurately model the complex interplay of information that characterizes human thought. This work addresses this limitation by introducing a flexible framework capable of integrating and processing multi-modal data, offering a potentially more realistic and robust model of human cognition. The architecture utilizes this unified neural space to perform cognitive task simulation and inference, demonstrating a significant advancement over existing approaches. The key innovations lie in the method of encoding and the architecture's capacity to dynamically adapt to novel cognitive demands.

title: Dynamic Quantum Error Correction Topology Network Construction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum error correction (QEC) network construction, termed "Dynamic Quantum Error Correction Topology Network Construction". The core claim centers around utilizing adaptive topology mapping techniques to enable real-time, lossless quantum data transmission across dynamic and heterogeneous physical topological networks without the need for pre-defined, fixed physical topologies. The proposed mechanism leverages the inherent redundancy within quantum error correction codes, dynamically adjusting transmission paths in response to changes in node connectivity within the network. This adaptive correction maintains the integrity of quantum information. The novelty lies in the system's ability to overcome the limitations of traditional QEC schemes which are heavily reliant on predefined topologies, particularly in the context of diverse and evolving physical networks. The theoretical framework is presented, detailing the key components and operational principles, highlighting the potential for significant advancements in scalable and robust quantum communication. The system's ability to adapt to changes in the network topology is crucial for practical applications.

abstract: This paper explores the application of topological quantum state evolution and manipulation, leveraging the inherent properties of topological structures, to develop a novel algorithm for precise state control. The research focuses on establishing a robust and efficient framework for simulating complex quantum states and performing precise control operations. This work introduces a new approach to quantum state evolution and manipulation, driven by the principles of topology, aiming to advance the capabilities of quantum computing. The core mechanism centers on the generation of complex topological structures that dynamically modify the system's state.

title: Quantum Network Security: A Multi-Party Computation Protocol Leveraging Quantum Key Distribution and Quantum State Secure Computation
abstract: This paper presents a novel protocol for secure multi-party computation (MPC) within a quantum network, integrating Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and quantum state secure computation techniques. The core objective is to enable multiple parties to collaboratively perform computations without revealing their individual inputs. The proposed protocol establishes a secure communication channel using QKD, guaranteeing the exchange of secret keys. Subsequently, a quantum state secure multi-party computation algorithm is employed, ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of the computation process. The utilization of quantum key distribution significantly enhances the security of the entire system, mitigating vulnerabilities associated with traditional MPC schemes. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the protocol's resilience against various attacks, providing a foundation for building robust and secure quantum network applications. The protocol's effectiveness hinges on the ability to maintain quantum coherence during the computational steps and accurately manage the quantum key distribution process. This research contributes to the advancement of secure quantum computing and communication technologies.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum State Simulation Parameter Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for quantum state simulation parameter optimization, driven by a self-adaptive module. Traditional quantum simulation often relies on manual parameter tuning, limiting the ability to effectively model complex quantum phenomena. Our approach introduces a dynamically adjusting parameter optimization module that leverages learned quantum state characteristics to refine simulation results. This leads to improved accuracy and efficiency in simulating quantum systems. The framework addresses a significant challenge in quantum simulation – the need for automated parameter adjustment – and offers a promising solution for tackling increasingly complex problems. The core mechanism centers around a self-learning algorithm that adapts the simulation parameters to best match the observed quantum state evolution. This results in a more robust and accurate simulation process.

abstract: Quantum computing stands on the precipice of transformative advancements, promising solutions to complex problems currently intractable for classical computers. The core claim is that this algorithm will drastically improve the accuracy of topology-based predictions, offering a significant step towards practical quantum applications.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Metric Quantification
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a profound challenge to our understanding of measurement and information. Traditional methods of quantifying entanglement, such as correlation measurements, often fail to capture the subtle nuances and interconnectedness of these fundamental phenomena. This paper introduces a novel metric, the 'Entanglement Flow,' designed to quantify the distance between entangled quantum systems, leveraging principles from quantum information theory and incorporating non-classical entanglement properties. The core mechanism centers on the concept of an entanglement flow, which dynamically tracks the evolution of entanglement across a system, providing a quantifiable measure of its connectedness. This approach moves beyond simple correlation analysis and offers a more sophisticated framework for characterizing the robustness and nature of quantum correlations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this metric through rigorous theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, suggesting it has the potential to significantly advance our comprehension of entanglement dynamics.

title: Algorithmic Stability Theory for Deep Generative Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithmic stability theory specifically tailored for deep generative models. The core challenge in training these models lies in predicting whether the training process will converge to a stable solution or diverge into instability. Current approaches often rely on empirical observations and heuristics. This work establishes a formal mathematical framework to analyze the dynamics of gradient descent optimization within deep generative models. We identify key factors contributing to instability, including vanishing and exploding gradients, as well as the presence of saddle points, and provide a theoretical understanding of their influence. The theory allows for the prediction of training convergence or divergence based on model architecture, learning rate schedules, and the specific generative task. This framework offers a significant advancement by moving beyond empirical debugging and provides a foundation for designing more robust and reliable training procedures for deep generative models.

title: Black Paca: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Alpacas
abstract: This paper proposes Black Paca, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the social behavior of alpacas, specifically their coordinated grazing patterns and decision-making processes. The algorithm leverages concepts of herd dynamics, information sharing, and adaptive strategy adjustment to achieve robust and efficient global optimization. Black Paca integrates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) with a novel 'herd influence' mechanism. The core of the algorithm centers around a population of 'agents' (particles) that collaboratively explore the search space. Each agent's movement is influenced by both its own best-known position and the collective intelligence of the herd, represented by a 'herd influence' vector. Adaptive adjustment of the herd influence vector, based on the algorithm's performance and the landscape's characteristics, allows the algorithm to dynamically shift between exploration and exploitation strategies. Experimental results on various benchmark functions demonstrate that Black Paca consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional optimization problems. The algorithm's adaptability and reliance on collaborative behavior are key factors contributing to its effectiveness. The mathematical formulation underlying the algorithm's key components, including the herd influence vector update, is presented in detail.

title: Beaufort's Bare-backed Fruit Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Beaufort's Bare-backed Fruit Bat Algorithm (BBFBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Macrodontia borealis*, commonly known as Beaufort's bare-backed fruit bat. These bats exhibit a unique and remarkably efficient foraging strategy, utilizing a 'contact-bounce' method to locate food sources. The BBFBA leverages this strategy through a combination of a probabilistic movement system, a 'bounce' mechanism for exploring the search space, and a 'contact' rule for exploiting promising regions. The algorithm employs a population-based approach with a dynamically adjusted inertia weight and a novel convergence criterion based on the bat's flight path. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the BBFBA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The results indicate that the BBFBA possesses strong exploration capabilities and efficiently converges towards optimal solutions, particularly in complex and high-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm's design reflects a careful consideration of the observed foraging dynamics of *Macrodontia borealis*, leading to a robust and adaptable optimization tool.

These bats exhibit a unique and remarkably efficient foraging strategy, utilizing a 'contact-bounce' method to locate food sources. The BBFBA leverages this strategy through a combination of a probabilistic movement system, a 'bounce' mechanism for exploring the search space, and a 'contact' rule for exploiting promising regions. The algorithm employs a population-based approach with a dynamically adjusted inertia weight and a novel convergence criterion based on the bat's flight path. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the BBFBA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The results indicate that the BBFBA possesses strong exploration capabilities and efficiently converges towards optimal solutions, particularly in complex and high-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm's design reflects a careful consideration of the observed foraging dynamics of *Macrodontia borealis*, leading to a robust and adaptable optimization tool.
