title: Quantum Walk-Based Routing Protocols for Wireless Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum walks to routing protocols within wireless networks. Traditional routing algorithms often struggle with efficiency and convergence speed, particularly in dynamic and complex network topologies. We propose a novel approach utilizing quantum walk principles to explore network connectivity and identify optimal routes. Our methodology employs a quantum walk algorithm to simulate network traversal, leveraging quantum superposition and interference to potentially achieve faster convergence and reduced latency compared to classical approaches. The core of the system relies on a discrete-time quantum walk on a graph representing the wireless network, where nodes are the walkers and edges represent communication links. The algorithm aims to minimize the walk length, effectively finding the shortest path between source and destination nodes. We present a theoretical framework and outline the key components of a quantum walk-based routing protocol. While this research focuses on the theoretical aspects and does not include experimental validation, it lays the foundation for future work exploring the practical feasibility and performance benefits of quantum walk routing in real-world wireless network scenarios.

title: ## Bartels's Spiny Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bartels's Spiny Rat" (BSR), inspired by the foraging strategies of the Bartels's spiny rat ( *Phenacella bartelsae*). These rats are renowned for their remarkable ability to locate and efficiently exploit sparse food resources in harsh desert environments. BSR leverages the principles of exploration and exploitation observed in the spiny rat's behavior, specifically its use of scent marking and sequential searching. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a virtual "territory" represented by a set of potential solutions. Each individual in the population continuously explores the search space, marking promising areas with "scents" (represented as numerical values), and sequentially moving towards the most concentrated scent regions. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's core components, including territory representation, scent marking, and movement strategy, are presented. The performance of BSR is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over existing metaheuristic algorithms. Key performance indicators include convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results suggest that BSR offers a robust and adaptable approach to complex optimization challenges.

title: Probabilistic Logic-Based Non-Deterministic Computation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computational paradigm based on probabilistic logic to address challenges inherent in traditional deterministic computing, particularly those arising from uncertainty and ambiguity. The core idea is to leverage the expressive power of probabilistic logic to model and manipulate information where definitive answers are absent. We introduce a computational model built upon probabilistic logic inference, coupled with Bayesian networks for robust uncertainty representation. This approach offers a fundamentally different way to approach computation, moving beyond the limitations of classical systems when dealing with incomplete, vague, or contradictory data. The key contributions of this work lie in the integration of probabilistic logic with non-deterministic computation, presenting a new computational framework capable of reasoning under conditions of inherent uncertainty. We explore the theoretical foundations and outline a potential implementation strategy. ---

title: 基于自适应的微观量子计算算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computing based on adaptive quantum state and entanglement manipulation. Traditional quantum algorithms often struggle to accurately simulate complex quantum systems, while adaptive quantum control offers the potential for increased computational efficiency. This work details the development of a new algorithm, termed "Dynamic Quantum Modulation" (DQM), which leverages self-adjusting parameters to dynamically control quantum states and entanglement, facilitating more precise and efficient simulation of quantum systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DQM through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of existing quantum computing methods. The core mechanism centers around intelligently adjusting quantum states and entanglement to achieve a higher level of simulation fidelity and computational speed.

title: Title: Self-Assembling Modular Logic Networks (SAML) - Continuous Evolution of Representation
abstract: This paper presents Self-Assembling Modular Logic Networks (SAML), a novel architecture for logical network representation designed for continuous evolution and self-improvement. Traditional logic networks are typically static, limiting their adaptability and potential for optimization. SAML leverages a meta-learning algorithm to iteratively refine the representation based on the outputs of previous computations, fostering a "living" logical network that adapts to changing data and requirements. The core mechanism centers around a hierarchical structure that allows for dynamic representation updates, ultimately enhancing the network's efficiency and robustness. We detail the design of the meta-learning algorithm, its implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the potential for SAML to outperform traditional approaches in various logical operation scenarios. Keywords: Self-Assembling, Modular Logic Networks, Meta-Learning, Representation Evolution, Dynamic Networks, Logical Networks.

title: ## The Pacific Squid-Inspired Adaptive Exploration and Exploitation Algorithm (SPEEA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Pacific Squid-Inspired Adaptive Exploration and Exploitation Algorithm (SPEEA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Pacific squid. The algorithm leverages the squid's ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on environmental conditions and individual experience, mimicking its cyclical movement patterns and selective adaptation. SPEEA incorporates three key mechanisms: a "contour current" component for exploration, a "prey density" component for exploitation, and an "adaptive weighting" mechanism to dynamically adjust the influence of these components. The algorithm maintains a population of potential solutions and iteratively refines them through a combination of global and local search strategies. The core innovation lies in the dynamically shifting balance between exploration and exploitation, guided by simulated environmental cues. This approach aims to achieve robust convergence and superior performance across a variety of optimization problems.

title: Formal Specification of Quantum Algorithms via Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum algorithms offer the potential for exponential speedups over classical algorithms for specific computational tasks. However, the inherent complexity and probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics pose significant challenges in verifying and understanding these algorithms. Traditional approaches, relying on simulations and theoretical arguments, often struggle to provide definitive proof of correctness and to guide the optimization of quantum circuits. This paper proposes a novel approach to formally specifying quantum algorithms by representing them using tensor networks. Tensor networks provide a powerful mathematical framework for describing multi-dimensional quantum states and operations, allowing for a precise and rigorous description of the algorithm's evolution. We demonstrate how tensor network techniques can be used to capture the unitary transformations that constitute a quantum algorithm, providing a foundation for automated verification and optimization strategies. The key contribution of this work is the application of tensor networks to the formal specification of quantum algorithms, addressing a critical gap in the field and paving the way for more robust and reliable quantum computation. The formal specification allows for the definition of the algorithm's state space and the evolution operator, enabling the application of mathematical techniques to analyze and improve the algorithm's performance.

title: 基于动态自律性结构的量子计算的几何优化
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic self-organization principles to quantum computation, proposing a novel geometric optimization framework. Traditional quantum algorithms often struggle with complex geometries, necessitating sophisticated optimization techniques. This work introduces a framework leveraging self-organization to efficiently explore and optimize geometric structures, ultimately achieving global optimization. The core mechanism centers around the inherent ability of self-organization to generate diverse solutions and adapt to changing conditions, offering a pathway toward more robust and efficient quantum algorithms. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its potential to address challenges in quantum circuit design and optimization.

title: ## Asian Garden Dormouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AGDMA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Asian Garden Dormouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AGDMA), motivated by the foraging behavior of Asian Garden Dormice. These animals exhibit a complex strategy for locating and exploiting food sources, characterized by exploration and exploitation phases with dynamic adjustments based on environmental cues. AGDMA leverages these principles to develop a new optimization technique. The algorithm incorporates a novel "dormouse trail" mechanism, simulating the trail-following behavior observed in these rodents, alongside an adaptive parameter control system inspired by their environmental responsiveness. The core of AGDMA is a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AGDMA through simulations and theoretical analysis, showcasing its ability to outperform existing metaheuristic algorithms in a range of benchmark problems. Specifically, we focus on problems exhibiting dynamic and multimodal landscapes, where traditional optimization methods often struggle. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results indicate that AGDMA presents a promising approach for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: A Physics-Based Architecture for General Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for General Artificial Intelligence (GAI) grounded in fundamental physical laws. Unlike current approaches reliant on symbolic logic or deep learning, this architecture leverages the inherent universality and predictability of physics—including thermodynamics, electromagnetism, and statistical mechanics—to achieve abstract reasoning and knowledge representation. The core claim is that intelligent behavior emerges naturally from the interaction of systems governed by these laws, offering a potentially more robust, explainable, and ultimately, generalizable solution to the GAI challenge. We outline the key components of the architecture, focusing on a process of 'physical simulation' as the basis for knowledge acquisition and inference. This approach addresses limitations of existing GAI systems by providing a foundation rooted in verifiable, objective reality, rather than learned patterns. The potential benefits of this framework, including improved robustness, interpretability, and the capacity for genuine discovery, are explored.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, the Quantum Entangled Neural Network (QENN), leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance prediction accuracy and generalization capabilities. We explore the potential of quantum entanglement to circumvent computational limitations inherent in traditional neural networks. The QENN utilizes a dynamically adjusted entanglement matrix to promote self-sustained quantum states, resulting in improved performance across a range of tasks. This work presents a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, highlighting its potential to advance neural network design. The core claim centers on the enhanced predictive power achieved through the manipulation of quantum entanglement. This advancement offers a promising pathway to create more robust and adaptable neural networks.

title: Title: Universal Quantum Constraint Optimization via Quantum Phase Fields
abstract: Quantum constraint optimization (QCO) aims to solve complex optimization problems by incorporating constraints as quantum states. Traditional approaches often face limitations in handling high-dimensional spaces and complex constraints. This paper introduces a novel quantum phase field technique designed to overcome these challenges, offering a fundamentally different approach to QCO. We propose a quantum algorithm that leverages the unique properties of quantum phase fields to simultaneously optimize multiple constraints, eliminating the need for conventional optimization techniques. This work presents a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the potential for significantly improved performance and efficiency in tackling challenging optimization problems across diverse fields.

title: Andrew Rebori's House Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bat Echo Location
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Andrew Rebori's House Bat" (ARHB), inspired by the echolocation behavior of bats. The algorithm leverages the dynamic exploration and exploitation strategies observed in bats navigating complex environments. ARHB integrates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms, focusing on mimicking bat's rotational movement, frequency modulation, and home-site selection. The algorithm utilizes a novel 'Echo Intensity' metric to assess the quality of solutions and guides the search process. The performance of ARHB is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability and adaptive nature. The key contributions of this work include the formulation of a bat-inspired algorithm with enhanced exploration and exploitation capabilities, the introduction of the Echo Intensity metric, and a comparative analysis of ARHB's performance against established metaheuristic techniques.

title: ## American Mastodon: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces American Mastodon, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm is inspired by the foraging behavior of American Mastodons, specifically their strategic searching and memory mechanisms for optimal food resource acquisition. American Mastodon integrates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Cauchy-Matrix Optimization (CMO) with a unique memory component mimicking the mastodon's recollection of successful foraging locations. The core of the algorithm revolves around a dynamic population of candidate solutions (particles) navigating a search space. Each particle's movement is governed by velocity updates influenced by both global and local best positions, along with the CMO component for exploration. Crucially, the algorithm incorporates a memory system, storing the locations of previously successful foraging sites, which significantly impacts the particle's future movement. This memory component is updated based on the fitness values of the particles and serves as a guide for the search. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for real-world applications. Experimental results indicate that American Mastodon exhibits robust convergence behavior and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms.

title: Amami Rabbit Metaheuristic Algorithm (ARMA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Amami Rabbit Metaheuristic Algorithm (ARMA), inspired by the unique foraging behavior of the Amami Rabbit. The algorithm incorporates elements of the rabbit's adaptability, spatial awareness, and opportunistic feeding habits into a new search strategy. ARMA utilizes a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism and a dynamic neighborhood structure. The algorithm aims to improve the convergence speed and global search capability compared to existing metaheuristic methods, particularly in complex, multi-dimensional optimization problems. The algorithm is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for various applications. Key aspects of the algorithm include a new position update rule, an adaptive inertia weight scheme, and a dynamically adjusted neighborhood structure. The results show that ARMA consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms like the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in terms of convergence rate and solution quality. Further research will explore the application of ARMA in real-world engineering and scientific problems.

title: Formal Modeling of Collective Intelligence using Petri Nets and Agent-Based Simulation
abstract: Collective intelligence (CI) refers to the emergent cognitive capabilities of groups of individuals. Capturing and understanding the underlying mechanisms driving CI remains a complex challenge. This paper proposes a novel framework for studying CI by integrating Petri nets, a formal modeling technique, with agent-based simulation (ABS), a dynamic simulation approach. The framework allows for the precise representation of system states and transitions, coupled with the simulation of individual agents' behaviors and their interactions. This combined approach facilitates the investigation of emergent patterns and the identification of key factors influencing CI. The core contribution is a methodology for systematically exploring the dynamics of CI systems, providing insights into the conditions under which CI arises and flourishes. The model utilizes a network of agents, each possessing a limited set of cognitive abilities, interacting according to predefined rules within a shared environment. The simulation explores how these interactions lead to the formation of collective knowledge and decision-making. This research aims to provide a robust theoretical foundation and practical tools for designing and understanding systems that leverage the power of collective intelligence.

title: Probability Space Geometry Logic
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of probability space geometry and logical reasoning, proposing a novel approach to representing and manipulating space through probabilistic models. The core concept revolves around a "probability geometric framework" that dynamically models objects and relationships by employing probability distributions. This framework facilitates robust logical inference, offering a departure from static, deterministic geometric models. The paper details the introduction of this framework, its mechanisms for representation, and its potential application to logical system construction.

title: ## The Flapping Sandpiper-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (FSASA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Flapping Sandpiper-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (FSASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Flapping Sandpipers. These birds exhibit a unique search strategy characterized by alternating periods of focused exploration and broader, more opportunistic exploitation. FSASA leverages this behavior by dynamically adjusting exploration and exploitation parameters based on the algorithm's current search state. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism, mimicking the sandpiper's intermittent flapping and gliding movements. The core innovation lies in a 'Flapping Rate' parameter, which regulates the balance between exploration and exploitation, and an 'Observation Range' parameter, controlling the scope of the search within a given solution. evidence.abstract: This paper introduces the Flapping Sandpiper-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (FSASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Flapping Sandpipers. These birds exhibit a unique search strategy characterized by alternating periods of focused exploration and broader, more opportunistic exploitation. FSASA leverages this behavior by dynamically adjusting exploration and exploitation parameters based on the algorithm's current search state. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism, mimicking the sandpiper's intermittent flapping and gliding movements. The core innovation lies in a 'Flapping Rate' parameter, which regulates the balance between exploration and exploitation, and an 'Observation Range' parameter, controlling the scope of the search within a given solution. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and conceptual underpinnings, outlining its potential for addressing complex optimization problems.

title: 基于量子信息的多尺度几何模型 - 拓扑信息整合
abstract: This paper presents a novel geometric model based on quantum information, designed to effectively integrate diverse spatial scales and achieve global optimization. The core concept revolves around utilizing quantum information processing and computation to harmonize geometric information across multiple scales, leading to a holistic optimization process. We introduce a framework that leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to represent and manipulate spatial relationships, enabling the model to identify optimal configurations and patterns. This research addresses the limitations of traditional geometric modeling by incorporating dynamic and spatially-aware optimization strategies. The model's architecture emphasizes the ability to capture and leverage intricate topological relationships inherent in complex geometries. This work provides a foundational framework for advanced geometric analysis and optimization, particularly within the context of spatial data and systems.

title: Quantum Spin Dynamics Simulation and Machine Learning Integration
abstract: Quantum Spin Dynamics Simulation and Machine Learning Integration Abstract This research investigates the integration of Quantum Spin Dynamics Simulation and Machine Learning to improve the accuracy of quantum system simulations. The core claim is to establish a robust framework for dynamic spin field simulation, utilizing machine learning algorithms to automatically learn the system's properties and train corresponding machine learning models. The research addresses the limitations of traditional simulation methods by leveraging the unique properties of quantum spin dynamics, offering a pathway towards more accurate and efficient simulations. The study will explore several key aspects, including the mapping of dynamic spin characteristics to machine learning models, training methodologies, and the validation of the resulting models. This work aims to advance the field of quantum simulation by combining established simulation techniques with the power of machine learning, ultimately contributing to a deeper understanding of quantum systems.

title: Title: Graph-Based Logical Reasoning as a General Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph-based logical reasoning model designed for automated inference and generalization from limited datasets. The model leverages Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to represent data and reasoning processes as graphs, facilitating efficient logical inference and expansion. The core mechanism centers around the ability to dynamically learn and extend logical rules from the data graph structure. This approach offers a significant advancement over traditional methods, enabling the model to automatically discover complex logical patterns and generalize to unseen scenarios. The paper details the model's architecture, training procedure, and performance evaluation on a range of logical reasoning tasks. We demonstrate that the proposed graph-based model achieves superior performance compared to existing approaches, particularly in scenarios requiring complex reasoning and generalization. The focus is on exploring how the graph structure can be leveraged to create a robust and adaptable logical inference engine.

We demonstrate the efficacy of this method in generating quantum states suitable for advanced quantum computing and quantum communication applications, offering a significant improvement in efficiency and security compared to traditional techniques. The study explores the potential of this technique to unlock new capabilities within quantum systems.

abstract: A human-evaluated corpus for benchmarking three Arabic NLP toolkits (Stanza, Farasa, CAMeL Tools) on POS tagging and lemmatisation. title: KOBONGOLA-Lite: Design and Prospective Evaluation Protocol for a Hybrid Offline French–Lingala Neural Translator on Resource-Constrained Smartphones
abstract: French and Lingala coexist in institutional, educational, and everyday communication in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where connectivity is uneven and entry-level Android devices remain widespread. This paper specifies KOBONGOLA-Lite, a proposed bidirectional offline French–Lingala neural translation architecture, and defines a prospective protocol for its implementation and confirmatory evaluation. The contribution is deliberately narrower than claims of first bidirectionality or first compression, because recent French–Lingala systems and AfriNLLB already cover these dimensions. KOBONGOLA-Lite instead coordinates four testable components: a governed and stratified Congolese corpus; explicit treatment of natural French–Lingala code-switching; a context-gated lexical mechanism with neural fallback; and physical-device validation of linguistic quality, memory, latency, energy, thermal behavior, reliability, and network silence. Interface prototypes specify the intended user workflows, while the compact encoder–decoder model, tokenizer, domain lexicon, span policies, hybrid reranker, and self-contained mobile bundle remain objects of prospective implementation and validation. The planned study separates external baselines from controlled internal ablations that isolate sequence-level distillation, lexical support, hybrid reranking, ONNX export, and dynamic INT8 quantization. The primary automatic endpoint is chrF++; complementary evidence comprises SacreBLEU, locally validated AfriCOMET, terminology and entity preservation, omission analysis, blinded human assessment, paired document-clustered bootstrap intervals, effect sizes, and an explicitly defined ten-test Holm family. No implementation or confirmatory performance result is claimed at this stage. The protocol establishes a falsifiable and reproducible basis for assessing offline neural machine translation in a low-resource African and edge-computing context.

title: Public Perception of National Athletes' Policies and Pensions: Sentiment Analysis on Instagram Social Media
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis persepsi publik terhadap kebijakan Dana Pensiun Atlet Nasional melalui teknik analisis sentimen pada komentar pengguna Instagram. Sebanyak 301 komentar dari enam akun Instagram dikumpulkan melalui web scraping dan diproses melalui tahapan pembersihan data, tokenisasi, serta klasifikasi sentimen menggunakan pendekatan lexicon-based IndoBERT. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan distribusi sentimen yang beragam, dengan sentimen negatif sebagai kategori terbanyak (118 komentar), disusul sentimen positif (106 komentar) dan netral (77 komentar). Dominasi sentimen negatif mengindikasikan adanya kekhawatiran publik terkait transparansi anggaran, kejelasan mekanisme, dan potensi ketidakadilan dalam distribusi manfaat. Sementara itu, sentimen positif mencerminkan dukungan terhadap upaya negara memberikan jaminan sosial sebagai bentuk penghargaan bagi atlet berprestasi. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa kebijakan telah memperoleh legitimasi nilai, namun legitimasi prosedural masih perlu diperkuat melalui komunikasi publik yang lebih transparan dan responsif. Penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa media sosial berfungsi sebagai ruang publik digital yang efektif dalam menangkap opini masyarakat secara real-time dan dapat menjadi dasar evaluasi kebijakan.

title: Reconstructing Explainability in Predictive Policing - From Outcome-Oriented XAI to Democratic Control of Input Data -
abstract: 예측치안(Predictive Policing)은 인공지능을 활용하여 범죄발생 가능성이 높은 지역이나 대상을 예측함으로써 경찰활동의 효율성을 제고하는 기술이다. 그러나 이러한 기술은 알고리즘의 불투명성, 편향, 책임소재의 불명확성 등으로 인해 민주적 정당성과 시민의 신뢰를 확보하는데 한계를 가진다. 최근 설명가능한 인공지능(XAI)이 이러한 문제의 해결방안으로 제시되고 있으나, 현재의 XAI는 알고리즘이 도출한 결과의 전제가 되는 기술적 설명에 초점을 둘 뿐, 결과의 전제가 되는 입력 데이터와 변수의 선정 과정은 설명의 대상으로 포함하지 못한다. 본 연구는 이러한 한계에 주목하여 설명가능성의 범위를 알고리즘의 출력 단계에서 입력 단계까지 확장해야 한다는 점에 이론적 근거를 제시하고 있다. 이를 위해 Tim Miller의 설명개념, 푸코의 권력-지식(앎)의 개념과 시간적 통치성, 하버마스의 민주적 담론 개념 등을 검토하여, 예측치안에서 활용되는 데이터와 변수의 선정은 단순한 기술적 설계가 아니라 사회적, 정치적 가치판단이 개입되는 과정이며, 민주적 통제와 사회적 정당성의 대상이 되어야 한다는 점을 논증하였다. 이를 통해, 본 연구는 XAI 개념 범위를 입력단계까지 확장하는 입력 설명가능성(Input Explainability) 개념을 제안한다.

title: Does Reasoning Mitigate Backdoor Attacks? A Neuro-Symbolic Perspective
abstract: Neuro-Symbolic (NeSy) AI has recently emerged as a novel paradigm to enable trustworthy AI, aiming at integrating sub-symbolic neural perception with grounded symbolic reasoning. The neuro-symbolic integration process that characterizes these models has been proven beneficial to achieve more transparent, explainable and efficient AI systems. Meanwhile, their properties under adversarial settings have been overlooked being frequently deemed robust-by-design. However, the neural-symbolic integration process they leverage constitutes an additional layer of complexity that may provide an attack entry-point. Therefore, in this paper, we claim that an in-depth investigation of the adversarial robustness of NeSy models is necessary and provide the first systematic evaluation of backdoor attacks against NeSy. To this end, we compare the most popular NeSy framework, namely DeepProbLog, against baseline neural networks across a total of eight backdoor settings and four reasoning tasks. Our experimental results show that while NeSy models are indeed more robust than their neural counterpart on average, their robustness vastly depend on the strictness of the reasoning process being enforced and its compatibility with the chosen adversarial target. The source code to reproduce our experiments is made available at https://github.com/marcoantoniocorallo/NeSy-Backdoor.

title: SlideBank: A Persistent Hierarchical Evidence Bank for Consistent Whole-Slide Reasoning
abstract: Whole-slide images (WSIs) are challenging for vision-language reasoning because diagnostically relevant morphology is sparse, heterogeneous, and distributed across gigapixel-scale images and multiple spatial resolutions. Existing WSI models and pathology agents can aggregate slide features or actively acquire evidence, but the information retained after exploration is often difficult to access semantically while preserving its connection to the original visual evidence. We introduce SlideBank, a training-free framework that represents each WSI as a persistent, concept-indexed, and spatially grounded evidence bank. SlideBank performs question-independent coarse-to-fine exploration to identify informative regions and multi-scale views, converts them into explicit morphological observations, and grounds pathology signals to their supporting patches and WSI coordinates. At inference time, questions are routed to relevant signals and evidence scales, and the linked global, regional, and patch evidence is integrated through confidence-based cross-level consensus. Experiments on WSI-VQA and SlideBench-BCNB show that with Patho-R1, SlideBank reaches 52.77% on WSI-VQA and with Quilt-LLaVA, it reaches 50.92% average accuracy on SlideBench-BCNB, while structured signal-guided retrieval consistently outperforms random evidence sampling. Reusing the same bank across repeated queries further achieves over 99% rephrasing consistency and substantially reduces amortized inference cost through persistent evidence reuse.

title: ScienceArena: Benchmarking LLMs on Latest Scientific Olympiad Competitions
abstract: Benchmark saturation and data contamination increasingly obscure genuine scientific reasoning in frontier LLMs. We introduce \textsc{ScienceArena}, an olympiad-style benchmark from thirteen public science competitions in physics, chemistry, and biology, including IPhO and IChO 2025--2026, IBO 2023, USAPhO 2026, and USNCO 2025. Its open-ended, multi-step problems use process-credit rubrics, making faithful scoring difficult. We build ScienceArena through an expert-audited digitization pipeline that converts official exams, figures, solutions, and rubrics into structured items verified by olympiad medalists. To scale evaluation beyond costly human grading, we calibrate LLM-as-judge against medalist ground truth on archived answers from five models across IPhO and IChO; two strong judges stay within one point of expert total scores. Medalist notes show that failures often stem from visual grounding, structure fidelity, and global problem control rather than missing terminology. Evaluating fourteen recent LLMs with interleaved solving, we find that top models obtain medal-equivalent rubric scores on several public international exams, while chemistry and long-horizon consistency remain key bottlenecks. We provide an interactive \href{https://science-arena.onrender.com/}{demo}.

evidence.title: ScienceArena: Benchmarking LLMs on Latest Scientific Olympiad Competitions
evidence.abstract: Benchmark saturation and data contamination increasingly obscure genuine scientific reasoning in frontier LLMs. We introduce \textsc{ScienceArena}, an olympiad-style benchmark from thirteen public science competitions in physics, chemistry, and biology, including IPhO and IChO 2025--2026, IBO 2023, USAPhO 2026, and USNCO 2025. Its open-ended, multi-step problems use process-credit rubrics, making faithful scoring difficult. We build ScienceArena through an expert-audited digitization pipeline that converts official exams, figures, solutions, and rubrics into structured items verified by olympiad medalists. To scale evaluation beyond costly human grading, we calibrate LLM-as-judge against medalist ground truth on archived answers from five models across IPhO and IChO; two strong judges stay within one point of expert total scores. Medalist notes show that failures often stem from visual grounding, structure fidelity, and global problem control rather than missing terminology. Evaluating fourteen recent LLMs with interleaved solving, we find that top models obtain medal-equivalent rubric scores on several public international exams, while chemistry and long-horizon consistency remain key bottlenecks. We provide an interactive \href{https://science-arena.onrender.com/}{demo}.

title: LookBack: Where and How to Score LVLM Responses via Visual Reference Usage
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) integrate visual perception with language generation, enabling responses that span image understanding and complex reasoning. However, LVLMs do not just inherit the text-level hallucinations; they also hallucinate against the image, producing fluent responses ungrounded in what they see. This makes LVLM response scoring inherently harder, and our diagnostics show that existing confidence-based metrics adopted from LLMs are insufficient for LVLMs. Specifically, removing the input image barely changes confidence-based selection, suggesting that output-space confidence primarily captures textual plausibility rather than agreement with the image. To address this gap, we propose LookBack, a training-free LVLM response scoring method that augments token likelihood with visual lookback score, a lightweight measure of how strongly each response token refers to image tokens. Across four benchmarks and three models, LookBack consistently improves Best-of-N selection over existing baselines with negligible additional overhead.

title: A NOVEL SELF-ADAPTIVE GRAPH TRANSFORMER FOR EXPLAINABLE BUFFER OVERFLOW VULNERABILITY DETECTION THROUGH DYNAMIC CODE SEMANTICS AND EVOLUTIONARY OPTIMIZATION
abstract: The Buffer overflow vulnerabilities continue to pose significant security challenges in modern software systems, frequently resulting in memory corruption, privilege escalation, denial-of-service attacks, and remote code execution. Traditional vulnerability detection techniques primarily rely on static code analysis, handcrafted features, or conventional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), which often struggle to capture dynamic execution semantics, long-range code dependencies, and complex structural relationships. These limitations can reduce detection accuracy, increase false-positive rates, and provide limited interpretability for security analysts. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a Self-Adaptive Graph Transformer Framework for Explainable Buffer Overflow Vulnerability Detection via Dynamic Semantic Graph Learning and Evolutionary Feature Optimization. The proposed framework constructs a unified semantic graph by integrating Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs), Control Flow Graphs (CFGs), Data Flow Graphs (DFGs), Program Dependence Graphs (PDGs), and dynamic execution traces, thereby preserving both structural and runtime semantic information. A Self-Adaptive Graph Transformer (SAGT) employing multi-head self-attention learns contextual relationships among code entities while adaptively assigning attention weights according to execution semantics and vulnerability relevance. An Evolutionary Feature Optimization (EFO) module identifies informative semantic graph features and eliminates redundant information. An Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) module further provides node-level and graph-level explanations, feature importance rankings, and vulnerability localization.The proposed framework is evaluated on publicly available software vulnerability datasets and benchmark repositories using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, and False Positive Rate (FPR). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms the evaluated static analysis, GNN, Transformer-based, and deep learning approaches in vulnerability detection performance. The integration of dynamic semantic graph learning, adaptive graph attention, evolutionary feature optimization, and explainable decision-making provides a promising framework for automated buffer overflow vulnerability detection and intelligent software security applications.

title: Replication data for "A Cost Model for Non-Bypassable Control Enforcement in Payment Systems: Reducing Verification Overhead in the Zero-Override Architecture": measurement testbed and cost-model analysis
abstract: Go measurement testbed, Python cost-model analysis, and configuration supporting the empirical characterization of verification cost in the Zero-Override Architecture (ZOA). The software measures per-hop and per-transaction verification cost, end-to-end latency, and multi-core throughput for a cryptographically attested control-enforcement pipeline, and fits the per-scheme cost laws (baseline O(n²), incremental and terminal O(n), batch O(n²) with a reduced constant) from which the verification-cost crossover is derived. It contains the six-component reference pipeline, microbenchmarks and the calibrator that renders per-transaction cost machine-independent, an end-to-end harness over mutual TLS, an independent conformance monitor that checks the enforcement properties (P1–P4), and the cost-law and cross-seed stability analyses. Ed25519 attestation verification uses the ed25519consensus library (vendored under third_party/ for offline builds). The testbed is written in Go 1.22 and the analysis in Python 3 (NumPy); results are emitted to a single canonical JSON store. Reproduction instructions are provided in README.

title: 基于自适应的动态机器学习特征选择
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic machine learning feature selection algorithm, termed "Adaptive Dynamic Feature Selection" (ADFS). The core idea is to treat feature selection as a machine learning process, dynamically adjusting feature selection strategies based on the data itself. Traditional feature selection methods are often static, limiting the algorithm's effectiveness. ADFS aims to surpass these limitations by incorporating data-driven optimization within the feature selection process. This paper details the algorithm's architecture, training procedure, and performance evaluation, demonstrating its ability to significantly enhance model performance across a range of datasets. The benefits of this approach include improved model accuracy, reduced overfitting, and enhanced interpretability. Keywords: Feature Selection, Machine Learning, Dynamic Feature Selection, Adaptive Learning, Optimization, Data-Driven.

title: 基于量子自适应的机器学习的噪声注入策略
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to machine learning model robustness utilizing a quantum-inspired adaptive noise injection strategy. Traditional noise injection methods often involve manual adjustments, leading to suboptimal results and limited adaptability. We introduce a quantum-driven mechanism that automatically adjusts the noise injection process, enabling the model to dynamically respond to perturbations and improve its resilience to adversarial attacks and data variations. The core of our approach lies in leveraging quantum entanglement to introduce subtle, controlled noise, fostering a more robust and adaptable learning process. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through extensive experimental analysis, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy and generalization performance compared to conventional techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Computing Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed computing architecture predicated on the precise control of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that by leveraging entanglement, it is possible to design a computing paradigm that surpasses the limitations of classical parallel computing. The proposed architecture utilizes entangled states to connect multiple quantum processors, enabling instantaneous state transfer and information sharing. This approach involves the development of new entanglement generation and control algorithms, optimized to manipulate quantum superposition and interference, thereby enhancing computational efficiency. The key innovation lies in moving beyond the bottleneck of classical communication inherent in traditional distributed systems. This architecture promises a fundamentally different approach to parallel computation, exploiting the unique properties of quantum mechanics. The presented framework offers a potential pathway towards scalable and highly efficient quantum computation, though significant technological challenges remain. The theoretical framework outlines the key components and operational principles of this new architecture.

title: Probabilistic Neural Network Training Based on Multi-Variable Optimization
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to training Probabilistic Neural Networks (PNNs) by leveraging the probabilistic nature of multi-variable optimization algorithms. Traditional PNN training often relies on gradient-based methods which can be sensitive to local minima and may not effectively explore the complex solution space. We propose integrating multi-variable optimizers, such as genetic algorithms or particle swarm optimization, into the PNN training process. The core idea is to exploit the inherent probabilistic exploration capabilities of these optimizers to guide the network's learning, ultimately leading to improved training outcomes. The methodology involves formulating the PNN training objective as a multi-dimensional optimization problem and employing the chosen multi-variable optimizer to iteratively adjust the network's parameters. We demonstrate, theoretically and conceptually, how this approach can overcome limitations of traditional training methods. This work lays a foundation for future research exploring the practical application and performance evaluation of this integrated framework. ---

title: Adaptive Multi-Scale Symbolic Learning Framework
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive multi-scale symbolic learning framework designed to automatically learn and dynamically adjust symbolic representations at varying scales based on the demands of a given task. The core of the framework leverages information bottleneck theory and autoencoders to construct a multi-scale symbolic representation generator. The system employs reinforcement learning or genetic algorithms to optimize the scale proportions, effectively addressing the limitations of existing symbolic learning methods which typically operate with fixed scales. The framework's adaptability significantly enhances its applicability across diverse tasks with varying levels of complexity. The proposed method aims to improve the efficiency and accuracy of symbolic representation learning by allowing the model to focus on the most relevant scales for each specific problem.

title: QuoNic: A Backend-Agnostic Quantum Middleware with Intelligent Scheduling and Dynamic-to-Static Compilation
abstract: Quantum computing frameworks---Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane, QPanda, and others---each provide their own circuit representations, compilation pipelines, and execution APIs. While individually capable, they are peers: code written for one cannot run on another without manual translation, and optimizations developed for one platform cannot benefit the rest. What is missing is not another framework, but a middleware layer that unifies them. We present QuoNic, a backend-agnostic quantum middleware that treats existing frameworks as compilation targets rather than competitors. QuoNic introduces three key innovations: (1) a vendor-neutral Intermediate Representation (IR) supporting high-level gate semantics that compile down to any backend's native instructions; (2) an intelligent scheduler that automatically selects the optimal backend and simulation method based on circuit features, achieving 1.30x median overhead relative to the best backend across 694 benchmark circuits; and (3) groverize(), a dynamic-to-static compilation pass that transforms repeat-until-success loops into coherent Grover circuits executable on any backend. Evaluated across 12 experiments covering cross-platform consistency, compilation optimization, and real-hardware validation on three quantum platforms, QuoNic achieves sub-millisecond compilation, consistent results across 8 backend configurations, and scales to 40 qubits for Clifford circuits.

title: Causal Discovery via Reinforcement Learning with Intervention Models
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal discovery utilizing reinforcement learning (RL) with intervention models. Traditional causal discovery methods often struggle with the inherent biases present in observational data and fail to explicitly model the impact of interventions. Our approach addresses these limitations by employing RL agents to simulate interventions on the observed data. These agents learn optimal intervention strategies by maximizing a reward function based on changes in the data distribution, effectively uncovering causal relationships. The core mechanism involves exploring different intervention scenarios, learning from the resulting data shifts, and ultimately identifying causal dependencies. We demonstrate the potential of this method to improve causal discovery accuracy compared to conventional techniques, particularly in scenarios with complex interdependencies. The key innovation lies in the integration of RL's ability to learn through trial and error with the explicit modeling of interventions, offering a more robust and informative pathway to causal inference.

title: Quantum Topologies and Adaptive Geometric Model Generation
abstract: Quantum Topologies (QT) offer a fundamentally different approach to geometric modeling compared to traditional methods, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum mechanics to create dynamic and adaptable representations. This paper explores the potential of QT as a novel method for generating geometric models, emphasizing their ability to dynamically adjust to the input data through a carefully orchestrated system of quantum operations. We propose a framework where the model's representation is continuously refined based on the data, enhancing its accuracy and performance. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing QT to create a self-organizing geometric structure, allowing for complex and nuanced representations. The resulting model exhibits enhanced robustness and adaptability, potentially surpassing the limitations of static geometric representations. This work investigates the theoretical underpinnings and practical implementation of QT for geometric modeling, highlighting its unique advantages and potential impact on various scientific disciplines.

title: Self-Adaptive Domain Theory: A Dynamic Parameterization Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive domain theory framework designed to enhance the modeling and optimization of complex systems, particularly neural networks and biological molecules. Traditional domain theory approaches are often static, limiting their ability to capture the dynamic complexity inherent in these systems. Our work proposes a dynamic parameterization mechanism, utilizing an adaptive "domain" to continuously adjust variable distributions, allowing for more accurate and flexible modeling. The core claim is that this framework offers a significant advancement in the representation and control of complex systems. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through illustrative examples, showcasing improved accuracy and robustness compared to static domain theory.

title: Self-Organizing Topological Neural Networks for Spatio-Temporal Data
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to building Topological Neural Networks (TNNs) designed specifically for handling spatio-temporal data. The core idea revolves around integrating a self-organizing mechanism within the TNN architecture. This mechanism dynamically adjusts the network's topology using a reinforcement learning algorithm, driven by gradient information and data similarity measures. The resulting Self-Organizing Topological Neural Network (SOTNN) aims to overcome limitations in traditional TNNs when dealing with complex, non-Euclidean datasets exhibiting intricate spatial and temporal correlations. The methodology leverages the inherent topological properties of the data to establish connections, allowing the network to learn patterns and relationships more effectively. Mathematical formulations detail the reinforcement learning process and the dynamic adjacency matrix update rules. This work presents a significant advancement in TNN design, offering a robust and adaptable framework for analyzing and modeling spatio-temporal data.

title: Cognitive Graph Networks for Multi-Modal Data Fusion
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Cognitive Graph Network (CGN) architecture designed to address the limitations of existing graph networks in effectively fusing multi-modal data. The core challenge in multi-modal data fusion lies in the disparate representations and complex relationships inherent across different modalities. Traditional graph networks often struggle to learn these intricate connections due to a lack of explicit cognitive reasoning and attention mechanisms. The proposed CGN incorporates attention modules to weigh the importance of different modalities and cognitive reasoning modules to infer high-level relationships between them. This allows the network to build a more robust and accurate representation of the fused data. We formally define the network architecture and its key components, outlining the mathematical operations involved in attention weighting and cognitive reasoning. The theoretical framework demonstrates a potential improvement in multi-modal data fusion performance compared to standard graph networks. The network aims to learn relationships defined by (xi, xj, αij), where xi and xj represent features from different modalities and αij is the learned attention weight. The cognitive reasoning module then operates on these weighted features using a rule-based system, represented by (Rk, yk), where Rk is a rule and yk is the output derived from applying the rule. The network's overall objective is to minimize the error between the predicted output and the ground truth, expressed as E = ∑i=1N ||yi - zi||2, where yi is the predicted output and zi is the ground truth. The design allows for flexible integration of new modalities and the incorporation of domain-specific knowledge. ---

title: # Black Agouti: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Black Agoutis
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Black Agouti, inspired by the foraging strategies of the Black Agouti (Dinarama pardata), a rodent known for its efficient and adaptive food searching behavior in complex environments. The algorithm leverages the Agouti's ability to rapidly assess food patches, prioritize exploration, and dynamically adjust its search radius based on environmental feedback. Black Agouti employs a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), utilizing a novel "Patch Assessment" mechanism to guide exploration and exploitation. The core of the algorithm resides in its adaptive search radius calculation, driven by a probability function that balances the cost of exploration with the potential reward of finding a superior solution. We present the algorithm's theoretical foundation, illustrate its key components, and demonstrate its performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its efficiency and adaptability compared to established metaheuristic techniques. evidence.abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Black Agouti, inspired by the foraging strategies of the Black Agouti (Dinarama pardata), a rodent known for its efficient and adaptive food searching behavior in complex environments. The algorithm leverages the Agouti's ability to rapidly assess food patches, prioritize exploration, and dynamically adjust its search radius based on environmental feedback. Black Agouti employs a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), utilizing a novel "Patch Assessment" mechanism to guide exploration and exploitation. We present the algorithm's theoretical foundation, illustrate its key components, and demonstrate its performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its efficiency and adaptability compared to established metaheuristic techniques. title: Title: Universal Quantum State Encoding (UQSE)
abstract: Quantum state encoding is a fundamental challenge in quantum information theory, and the ability to represent a diverse range of physical phenomena with a single encoding scheme represents a significant advancement. Current methods often suffer from inherent limitations in the number of states they can accommodate, hindering the exploration of complex quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel approach, Universal Quantum State Encoding (UQSE), which leverages a dynamically adjustable state vector modulation algorithm to achieve a significantly expanded state representation. UQSE offers the potential for a much more versatile and adaptable encoding scheme, opening avenues for a broader range of quantum phenomena. The core mechanism of UQSE involves iteratively refining the state vector based on input data, enabling a more flexible representation of quantum states. This paper will detail the theoretical underpinnings of UQSE, present a preliminary implementation, and discuss its potential applications and future directions.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre and fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a tantalizing pathway to information transfer beyond the limitations of classical physics. This paper explores the theoretical underpinnings, design considerations, and potential challenges associated with implementing this advanced communication paradigm. The core claim is that this protocol can facilitate the transmission of information across unprecedented distances, potentially revolutionizing secure communication and fundamental scientific research.

title: Dynamic Neuron Topology Modeling
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic nature of neural network topology, proposing a novel framework for modeling how neuronal connections evolve over time. The core claim is that neural network connectivity is not static but rather undergoes dynamic changes, profoundly impacting its functionality and adaptability. The proposed mechanism utilizes a machine learning-based algorithm to analyze real-time neural activity patterns, subsequently adjusting connection strengths and topology to mimic self-organization and adaptation within biological neural networks. The research addresses a significant gap in current modeling approaches, which often assume static connections. The developed framework offers a more realistic representation of neural networks, potentially leading to improved understanding and design of artificial neural networks. This work focuses on the theoretical development and algorithmic design, without experimental validation, and provides a foundation for future research in dynamic neural network modeling. The key equations and notation used throughout this paper are as follows: xi represents the activation of neuron *i*, wij represents the synaptic weight between neuron *i* and neuron *j*, σ(xi) represents the activation function for neuron *i*, η represents the learning rate, and λ represents a regularization parameter. The goal is to create a system that can dynamically adapt to changing inputs and maintain optimal performance.

title: Title: Non-Standard Geometric Regularity for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-standard geometric regularity to machine learning models, aiming to enhance generalization and robustness. Traditional regularization methods often struggle with complex data distributions and can limit model expressiveness. We introduce a novel geometric regularity structure, termed "Adaptive Geometric Regularity," that dynamically adjusts the model's geometric structure during training, offering a potential improvement over existing techniques. This adaptive approach, combined with a novel loss function, addresses the challenges of overfitting and promotes better model performance on unseen data. The paper details the implementation of this structure, provides a theoretical analysis of its effectiveness, and demonstrates its efficacy through simulations and a preliminary case study. We conclude with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: Based on Quantum State Reorganization for Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational model predicated on quantum state reorganization. The core idea centers around leveraging the inherent transformational properties of quantum states to achieve efficient computation. We present a detailed algorithmic design capable of precisely controlling the manipulation of quantum states through reorganization, ultimately enabling the execution of specified computational tasks. This approach represents a nascent quantum computing paradigm with substantial potential. The model aims to overcome limitations inherent in traditional quantum algorithms by offering a fundamentally different method for problem-solving. We explore the mathematical underpinnings of the proposed system, focusing on state vector representations, unitary transformations, and the principles of quantum state rearrangement. This work lays the groundwork for future research into this promising area, aiming for scalability and practical applications.

title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit Design – Optimizing for Circuit Length and Fidelity
abstract: Quantum circuit design presents a significant challenge due to the inherent complexity of quantum systems and the need to balance circuit length with fidelity. Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameter settings, limiting the potential for substantial improvements. This paper introduces an adaptive quantum circuit design algorithm leveraging reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust circuit parameters during synthesis, optimizing for both length and fidelity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a comprehensive analysis of circuit designs and performance metrics, highlighting its potential to significantly enhance both circuit length and overall quality. The core mechanism centers around a reinforcement learning agent that learns to optimize circuit parameters based on the current state of the circuit, leading to more efficient and robust designs.

title: ## Red Shrimp Mimic Metaheuristic Algorithm (RMSMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Red Shrimp Mimic Metaheuristic Algorithm (RMSMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of red shrimp (*Parastrombus cornutus*). Red shrimp exhibit a unique strategy for finding food sources, employing a combination of exploration and exploitation, particularly utilizing a "puff" strategy to identify promising areas. RMSMA leverages this behavior by introducing a 'puff' mechanism within a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework. The algorithm maintains a population of particles, each representing a potential solution. A 'puff' radius is dynamically adjusted based on the diversity of the population, encouraging exploration when diversity is low and focusing on promising areas when diversity is high. The inertia weight, cognitive and social coefficients are also dynamically adjusted based on the 'puff' radius, allowing the algorithm to adapt to the complexity of the search space. The core innovation lies in the adaptive control of the exploration-exploitation balance, mimicking the shrimp's intelligent foraging. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical foundation, outlining its key components and operational rules, and presents a conceptual framework for its potential application in various optimization problems.

title: Title: Non-Linear Harmonic Analysis for Cryptography (NLHA-C)
abstract: This paper introduces Non-Linear Harmonic Analysis for Cryptography (NLHA-C), a novel technique for analyzing the security of cryptographic systems by leveraging the power of non-linear harmonic analysis. Traditional cryptanalysis primarily relies on linear vulnerabilities, while NLHA-C aims to identify weaknesses arising from subtle, non-linear effects within encryption algorithms, offering a proactive approach to security assessment. The core of this research involves developing a new framework for quantifying and exploiting these subtle vulnerabilities. We will demonstrate the effectiveness of NLHA-C through a series of theoretical analyses and preliminary experimental investigations, showcasing its potential to uncover previously unnoticed weaknesses in established cryptographic protocols. This work represents a significant advancement in the field of cryptanalysis, shifting the focus towards identifying vulnerabilities tied to non-linear dynamics.

title: ## Arnham Tomb Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Bat Foraging
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Arnham Tomb Bat" (ATB), inspired by the foraging behavior of bats in the Arnham cave system. The algorithm leverages the dynamic exploration and exploitation strategies observed in bat populations, adapting them to solve complex optimization problems. ATB incorporates key elements of the bat algorithm, including position representation, velocity adjustment, and target detection, but introduces a significant modification: a "tomb" concept simulating the bats' avoidance of unproductive regions within the cave. This "tomb" mechanism dynamically restricts the search space, significantly improving convergence speed and preventing premature convergence to local optima. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its efficacy and adaptability. The core mathematical formulation of ATB is presented, detailing the update equations for position, velocity, and the tomb probability. The results highlight ATB's potential as a robust and efficient solution for a variety of optimization challenges.

title: Cognitive Architectures for Explainable AI – A Formal Framework
abstract: The increasing deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems in critical applications necessitates a shift from "black box" models to explainable AI (XAI). Current XAI techniques often provide post-hoc explanations that lack genuine understanding and can be easily manipulated. This paper proposes a formal framework for XAI based on cognitive architectures. The core idea is that by modeling human reasoning processes within a formal architecture, we can create AI systems whose decision-making is inherently transparent and traceable. This framework utilizes a modular architecture comprising perception, memory, and decision-making components. The architecture is designed to allow for the explicit tracking and interpretation of reasoning steps, offering a deeper level of explanation than traditional XAI methods. The paper details the formalization of this architecture, emphasizing the mathematical foundations for reasoning and explanation generation. We introduce key concepts such as belief revision, rule-based systems, and probabilistic reasoning within the architecture to simulate cognitive processes. The ultimate goal is to establish a robust foundation for building truly explainable AI systems that align with human understanding.

title: ## The Prairie Cat Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (PCIMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Prairie Cat Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (PCIMA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies and movement patterns of the prairie cat (*Felis nebulosa*). The algorithm leverages the prairie cat's adaptive exploration and exploitation behavior, specifically its ability to dynamically adjust its search range based on environmental cues and prey availability, to improve the efficiency of solving complex optimization problems. PCIMA employs a multi-layered search space representation, mimicking the prairie cat's spatial awareness, and utilizes a dynamic adjustment mechanism for both exploration and exploitation phases, informed by a 'prey density' concept analogous to the animal's resource assessment. The algorithm incorporates a 'stalking' phase, simulating the cat's focused pursuit of prey, and a 'retreat' phase, representing its avoidance of unfavorable areas. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulations, and conceptual underpinnings, highlighting its potential advantages in navigating challenging optimization landscapes.

title: Emergent Behavior Modeling in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the phenomenon of emergent behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) systems. Emergent behavior, characterized by complex and often unexpected behaviors arising from the interactions between multiple agents, represents a significant challenge and opportunity in MARL research. This work proposes a framework for modeling these emergent behaviors, leveraging mathematical modeling and simulation techniques. We analyze MARL systems with varying parameters to identify patterns and establish corresponding behavioral models. The core claim is that a detailed understanding of these interactions can reveal the underlying rules governing emergent behavior. The research focuses on the intricate interplay between agents, contributing to a deeper comprehension of how complex strategies emerge from simple learning algorithms. This work provides a foundation for designing more robust and predictable MARL systems.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Reinforcement Learning for Automated Theorem Proving
abstract: This research investigates a novel approach to automated theorem proving by integrating neural networks and symbolic reasoning through reinforcement learning. The core idea is to leverage the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks to translate natural language queries into formal symbolic representations, while employing a reinforcement learning agent to strategically navigate the complex proof space. This framework aims to overcome limitations of traditional automated theorem provers by providing an adaptive and intelligent exploration mechanism. The system's performance is evaluated based on its ability to generate correct proofs for a range of mathematical theorems. The key innovation lies in the active guidance of the proof search process, enhancing both the automation and adaptability of the theorem proving system. The system utilizes a neural network encoder, a reinforcement learning agent, and a symbolic proof planner. The objective function for the reinforcement learning agent is designed to maximize proof progress, considering factors such as the reduction of logical clauses and the achievement of a valid proof structure. Experimental results demonstrate the potential of this neuro-symbolic approach for tackling complex mathematical problems.

title: ## Andersen's Slit-faced Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bat Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Andersen's Slit-faced Bat (ASB), inspired by the foraging behavior of Andersen's Slit-faced Bats ( *Myotis andrenii*). These bats exhibit a unique hunting strategy, utilizing a "slit-faced" foraging pattern characterized by rapid, erratic movements and a reliance on auditory cues. ASB leverages these characteristics to develop an efficient and robust optimization algorithm. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, a novel pulse frequency modulation mechanism mimicking the bat's auditory navigation, and a localized search strategy based on the bat's flight path. Mathematical formulations detailing the core components of ASB, including the pulse frequency, flight speed, and position update rules, are provided. The algorithm is demonstrated through several benchmark test functions, showcasing its competitiveness against established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization. The results highlight the potential of ASB as a powerful tool for solving complex optimization problems.

title: ## Ant Colony Optimization Inspired Adaptive Search (ACoIAS)
abstract: This paper introduces Ant Colony Optimization Inspired Adaptive Search (ACoIAS), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of ants. ACoIAS combines the strengths of Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) with adaptive parameter control mechanisms to enhance its exploration and exploitation capabilities, particularly in complex and dynamic optimization landscapes. The algorithm utilizes a novel "pheromone decay rate adaptation" mechanism, dynamically adjusting the pheromone decay rate based on the diversity of the current solution set, promoting effective exploration in regions with high solution diversity and efficient exploitation in regions with low diversity. Furthermore, ACoIAS incorporates a "local search strategy" inspired by ant trail reinforcement, encouraging ants to converge towards promising solutions within their local neighborhood. The core innovation lies in the adaptive nature of both the pheromone decay and the local search, allowing the algorithm to dynamically adjust its search strategy to better suit the characteristics of the optimization problem. title: ##基于多智能体模拟的城市规划与管理
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Multi-Agent Simulation (MAS) for urban planning and management. The core claim is to leverage MAS to model and simulate the complex processes involved in urban development, ultimately leading to predictive analysis and optimization of urban planning strategies. The proposed mechanism centers around representing various urban elements as intelligent agents, enabling them to learn urban development patterns through interaction with the environment and to achieve coordinated planning and management through a multi-agent collaborative framework. The research introduces a novel approach to urban planning by utilizing MAS, offering potential new insights into urban development pathways. The presented model focuses on key aspects such as transportation networks, land use, and resource allocation, employing agent-based modeling to capture the emergent behaviors arising from the interactions between these elements. This approach allows for the testing of various planning interventions and policies within a simulated environment, providing valuable data for decision-makers. The paper outlines the key components of the MAS framework, discusses the challenges associated with its implementation, and presents a preliminary case study illustrating its potential application.

title: ## Amazonian Sac-winged Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Sac-winged Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (SBIMA)," designed to tackle complex optimization challenges. The inspiration for SBIMA stems from the foraging behavior of the Amazonian sac-winged bat ( * Macroglossus perlatus*), particularly their unique echolocation and cooperative searching strategies. The algorithm leverages the bat's ability to adapt its flight parameters – frequency and amplitude – based on environmental feedback to dynamically adjust its search process. Specifically, SBIMA incorporates a frequency-amplitude modulation scheme mimicking bat echolocation, combined with a cooperative search mechanism inspired by bat colony behavior. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The core components of SBIMA include an adaptive frequency and amplitude parameterization, a cooperative search strategy based on bat interactions, and an objective function evaluation mechanism. The performance of SBIMA is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its efficacy in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that SBIMA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, offering a potentially valuable tool for addressing diverse complex optimization scenarios.

title: ## Alpine Field Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Alpine Field Mouse Algorithm" (AFMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Alpine Field Mice. These mice exhibit remarkable adaptability to challenging environments and efficient resource acquisition strategies. AFMA leverages these characteristics to tackle complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of mouse foraging, including path planning, resource evaluation, and adaptive movement strategies, into a simulated annealing framework. We detail the algorithm's core components, including the 'territory' concept, 'resource' scoring, 'movement' rules, and 'adaptation' mechanisms. Mathematical formulations are presented to illustrate the core principles. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential application to various optimization scenarios. The aim of this work is to provide a robust and efficient approach to optimization problems where traditional metaheuristics may struggle, particularly those with complex constraints and dynamic environments. The performance of AFMA is evaluated through comparative analysis against established algorithms, showcasing its ability to converge towards optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time.

title: ## Aldabra Flying-fox Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AFIMA)
abstract: This paper presents Aldabra Flying-fox Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AFIMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Aldabra flying-foxes (Pteraops alfieri). These bats exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources within a complex, dynamic environment. AFIMA leverages this behavior by incorporating concepts such as flocking, foraging strategies, and social interaction into its search process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a virtual "flock" of individuals that dynamically adjust their positions and movement based on local food availability and the collective behavior of the group. Specifically, AFIMA utilizes a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) core, enhanced with a novel 'Social Influence' mechanism and a 'Foraging Radius' parameter to mimic the bats' exploration and exploitation strategies. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods. The key contributions of this work include the formalization of the bats' foraging dynamics into an algorithmic framework and a demonstration of its efficacy in solving complex optimization challenges. The performance metrics considered include convergence speed, solution quality (measured by the objective function value), and computational efficiency.
